blocks.ostepDetail:
Module 1

Core 1: financial accounting and reporting

  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22
  • About eight weeks of online learning with weekly assignments, 15 to 20 hours of study a week, and a mandatory two-day workshop. A two-day orientation workshop precedes Core 1. W22W29
  • Ends with a four-hour, in-person exam of objective-format questions and short cases. CPA Canada sets the dates and marks every exam nationally. W28W29
  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22
OntarioModule fee $1,525 + HST. Exams are written at centres across Ontario. ON18ON20
QuebecNational Program: online modules with in-class workshops, exams at a centre in Montréal, and a coach for each group of 6 to 10. University students take equivalent courses instead. QC16QC17QC20
WestModule fee $1,630 + GST. Final session Jan 23 – Mar 24, 2027; last exam, rewrite only, Jun 30, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,910 + HST. A 20-week extended version was offered alongside the eight-week one. A10
blocks.ostepAll:
All 8 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: a degree, 120 credit hours and 14 prerequisite courses

  • A degree and 120 credit hours of post-secondary education, plus 14 prerequisite courses: nine core and five non-core. W27W30
  • Grades: at least 60% in each core course, 50% in each non-core course, and a 65% average across the core courses. W27ON18ON19
  • Missing prerequisites can be taken at a post-secondary institution, through the profession’s own preparatory courses, or a mix of both. W27ON19
  • Preparatory courses are not part of the certification program itself; they exist to fill prerequisite gaps. W33
OntarioCPA Ontario runs its own preparatory courses (PREP). A four-year degree, or 120 credit hours, is required. The last PREP exam is December 2026. ON19ON18ON14
QuebecA recognized bachelor’s degree includes all the prerequisite courses for admission to CPA PEP. Then comes either a university graduate program (minimum average 2.8/4.3, set by each university) or the National Program delivered by the Order. QC23QC16QC18
WestCPAWSB preparatory courses cover all 14 prerequisites; at least one core course per competency area must be within 10 years. Applicants without a degree can use an eight-year “mature status” route. Courses end December 2027. W27W30
AtlanticCPA Atlantic preparatory courses cost $850 per core course and $655 per non-core course and run until December 2027. Applications to CPA PEP itself have closed. A11A10
Step 2 · Module 1

Core 1: financial accounting and reporting

  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22
  • About eight weeks of online learning with weekly assignments, 15 to 20 hours of study a week, and a mandatory two-day workshop. A two-day orientation workshop precedes Core 1. W22W29
  • Ends with a four-hour, in-person exam of objective-format questions and short cases. CPA Canada sets the dates and marks every exam nationally. W28W29
  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22
OntarioModule fee $1,525 + HST. Exams are written at centres across Ontario. ON18ON20
QuebecNational Program: online modules with in-class workshops, exams at a centre in Montréal, and a coach for each group of 6 to 10. University students take equivalent courses instead. QC16QC17QC20
WestModule fee $1,630 + GST. Final session Jan 23 – Mar 24, 2027; last exam, rewrite only, Jun 30, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,910 + HST. A 20-week extended version was offered alongside the eight-week one. A10
Step 3 · Module 2

Core 2: management accounting, planning and control

  • Core 2 centres on management accounting, planning and control. A10
  • Same format as Core 1: about eight weeks online, a two-day workshop and a four-hour exam. W29W22W28
  • Core 1 must be completed before Core 2 unless the two are taken together on the fast-track pathway, which takes about 40 hours a week. W28W29
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Final Core 2 exam September 2027. ON18ON14
QuebecEach National Program module costs $1,747.62 with taxes. Last offering Jul 24 – Sep 17, 2027. QC19QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final session Jul 24 – Sep 22, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 4 · Modules 3 and 4

Two elective modules: the specialization choice

  • Candidates choose two of four: Assurance, Taxation, Finance and Performance Management. The focus is depth. W22
  • Both core modules must be complete before the electives. Each elective ends with its own four-hour exam. W29W28
  • Public accounting requires the Assurance and Taxation electives. W22ON21
  • The elective choice also shapes the CFE: Day 2 is written in one of four roles that mirror the electives. ON21W32
OntarioEach elective $1,450 + HST. Final elective exams March 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecGraduate-program students choose two of the four as university courses; the Assurance and Taxation courses are needed for the CPA auditor designation. QC16QC18
WestEach elective $1,470 + GST. Final session Jan 29 – Mar 29, 2028; all elective exams fall on the same day, so candidates are told to plan for one. W31W25
AtlanticEach elective $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 5 · Module 5

Capstone 1: the integrative team case

  • Teams work through one large business case, building strategic leadership, teamwork and communication skills. The same case is the basis of Day 1 of the CFE. W22W32
  • There is no exam. Candidates are evaluated on a group report and an oral presentation to a panel. W32QC17
  • Two electives must be passed before Capstone 1. W28
  • Each Capstone 1 case is used for two CFE sittings. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended immediately before the CFE: Capstone 1 from May for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecAssessed on three components: individual contribution to teamwork, the group report and the oral presentation. Last offered spring 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering May 27 – Jul 28, 2028, presentations Jul 21–27. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 6 · Module 6

Capstone 2: preparation for the Common Final Examination

  • Applies everything learned so far to complex, highly integrative practice cases. W22W32
  • No module exam. Candidates must complete a set number of practice cases to become eligible for the CFE. W32
  • Practice cases use the candidate’s declared elective role, the same role tested on Day 2 of the CFE. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended from July for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecNo exam; once complete, the candidate can write the CFE. Last offered summer 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering starts Aug 5, 2028. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 7 · National exam

The Common Final Examination (CFE)

  • A three-day, 13-hour examination: Day 1 four hours, Day 2 five hours, Day 3 four hours. First-time writers must attempt all three days in the same sitting. W21W32
  • Day 1 is based on the Capstone 1 case. Day 2 tests depth in one of four elective roles together with Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. Days 2 and 3 together test depth and breadth, and the three-day CFE requires breadth across all six technical competencies. W32ON21ON22W21ON22
  • Three attempts. Unlike module exams, the CFE cannot be deferred. QC17QC1W21
  • Only two sittings remain: Sep 8–10, 2027 and Sep 26–28, 2028. There are no May sittings. W25QC11
OntarioFee $2,050 + HST for all three days. Final CFE September 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecFee $1,997.12 with taxes. Written in French or English. QC19QC17
WestFee $2,070 + GST. First-attempt pass rate in 2025 was 69.8% (CPABC). W31BC1
AtlanticFee $1,940 + HST. A10
Step 8 · Finish

Membership: education, the CFE and practical experience

  • The certification program has three parts: CPA PEP, the CFE and 30 months of paid practical experience. W33BC1
  • Experience does not have to be finished before the CFE; it can be completed at any time within the program time limit. W16
  • A public accounting licence needs the Assurance and Taxation electives, the Assurance role on the CFE with depth in Assurance and Financial Reporting, and chargeable hours in audit or assurance. ON21
OntarioDeregistration deadlines: six years after starting CPA PEP unless the CFE has been attempted; seven years to finish experience; ten years after first registration. ON23
QuebecThe whole path must be completed within seven years of registering as a candidate. Practical experience is 24 months. QC16QC9
WestSix years for CPA PEP and seven years overall, with up to 24 months of approved leave. W23
AtlanticUp to six years for CPA PEP and the CFE. A10

blocks.opaths:
Graduate diploma in the summer, then a firm

The Ontario diploma design: 20 of the 42 Ontario rows on CPA Canada’s list cover only Core 1, Core 2 and two electives, the largest group (our count). The two diplomas cited here run 13 weeks. The timeline assumes full-time work starts in September; the graduate then takes Capstone 1 from May and Capstone 2 from July in CPA PEP, as CPA Ontario recommends for a September CFE, and writes the CFE that September. N4U4U7ON17

Time off around Capstone 2 and the CFE is arranged with the employer; CPAWSB notes the program assumes only the few days between Capstone 2 and the CFE. One university says Capstone 1, Capstone 2 and the CFE can be completed in five months. W32U16

Master’s program covering all six modules

Some master’s programs include both Capstones, so their graduates go straight to the CFE. In the West the two accredited master’s programs run over two summers, with work in between; Waterloo’s MAcc took eight months. N4U34X1U2

CPA PEP part time while working

The route with no university program: one module per session, which most candidates take while working full time. The most common time to finish the six modules is 16 to 24 months. W29

University graduate program in Quebec

A DESS replaces all six modules; HEC’s current program is a 16-month cohort. Students fit a work term inside the program and must also pass the CFE, which the Order’s calendar lists for September. Quebec requires 24 months of experience. N4QC21QC18QC11QC9

blocks.stepDetail:
Module 1

Module 1: Foundational Development

  • Develops the Specific, Foundational and Sub-Foundational Competencies and begins the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies. Experience reporting can begin when this module starts. N2W5
  • You must pass the module’s own assessments before you can sit its exam. W5ON2
  • Foundational Development Exam: 5 hours. 50 objective-format questions (33%) plus 4 to 8 testlets (67%). Pass requires sufficiency on Financial Reporting and Management Decision-Making combined, and overall. Handbooks, Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act available. Non-disclosed. N1
  • This is the only module exam that is not part of the three-part Professional Final Exam. W6W16
Ontario14 weeks, delivered by accredited universities, not CPA Ontario: online through Executive Education at Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey (self-paced, minimum 15 hours a week), or in-person in a graduate program. First online offering May 31, 2027. Accredited in-person programs may deliver their own equivalent of the module exam. ON2ON13
Quebec16 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online in the Order’s program; or equivalent university courses. Order modules begin May 2027. The exam is run by the universities for graduate-program candidates and by the Order for its own candidates. QC3QC1
WestOnline, weekly submissions, with a two-day in-person orientation workshop. Standard track (about 20 h/week) or flexible track (about 10 h/week). First start May 15, 2027; registration opens Feb 1, 2027. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. W5W7W8
AtlanticSame design and dates as the West: first start May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. The schedule lists the two-day orientation workshop as online. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. A2
blocks.stepAll:
All 7 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: degree, credits, and proof of accounting knowledge

  • A degree (or equivalent), at least 120 credit hours, a minimum GPA set by the region, and evidence of good character. ON9W2A2
  • Accounting and business knowledge is shown one of two ways: recognized post-secondary coursework, or passing the Knowledge Assessment. N2ON9W3
  • Knowledge Assessment: 150 objective-format questions in 5 hours. Part A is 3 hours (90 questions across eight topic areas), Part B is 2 hours (60 questions, half Financial Reporting and half Management Decision-Making). No reference materials. To pass you need sufficiency on Financial Reporting, on Management Decision-Making, and overall. N1
  • Offered three times a year. First sitting: March 23, 2027. ON4W7W4
OntarioMinimum 70% GPA across the 120 credit hours. Knowledge is shown by the 15 CPA Qualifying Courses (7 named + 8 other business courses) or the Knowledge Assessment, completed within three years before enrolling in Foundational Development. Up to three Knowledge Assessment attempts. Non-degree route: eight years of relevant experience. ON9ON10ON11ON12
QuebecA bachelor’s degree recognized by the Order (or the equivalence process), obtained within the five years before applying. No minimum average for the program delivered by the Order; universities set their own. QC1
WestMinimum 65% GPA on the most recent 60 credit hours. Knowledge is 45 credit hours (21 in required topics + 24 other) or the Knowledge Assessment; currency window is five years. Non-degree applicants can use an eight-year “advanced experience” pathway. W2W11
AtlanticMinimum 65% GPA. Same 45-credit-hour rule (21 + 24) with one course inside five years, or the Knowledge Assessment (result valid five years). A2A6A3
Step 2 · Module 1

Module 1: Foundational Development

  • Develops the Specific, Foundational and Sub-Foundational Competencies and begins the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies. Experience reporting can begin when this module starts. N2W5
  • You must pass the module’s own assessments before you can sit its exam. W5ON2
  • Foundational Development Exam: 5 hours. 50 objective-format questions (33%) plus 4 to 8 testlets (67%). Pass requires sufficiency on Financial Reporting and Management Decision-Making combined, and overall. Handbooks, Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act available. Non-disclosed. N1
  • This is the only module exam that is not part of the three-part Professional Final Exam. W6W16
Ontario14 weeks, delivered by accredited universities, not CPA Ontario: online through Executive Education at Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey (self-paced, minimum 15 hours a week), or in-person in a graduate program. First online offering May 31, 2027. Accredited in-person programs may deliver their own equivalent of the module exam. ON2ON13
Quebec16 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online in the Order’s program; or equivalent university courses. Order modules begin May 2027. The exam is run by the universities for graduate-program candidates and by the Order for its own candidates. QC3QC1
WestOnline, weekly submissions, with a two-day in-person orientation workshop. Standard track (about 20 h/week) or flexible track (about 10 h/week). First start May 15, 2027; registration opens Feb 1, 2027. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. W5W7W8
AtlanticSame design and dates as the West: first start May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. The schedule lists the two-day orientation workshop as online. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. A2
Step 3 · Module 2

Module 2: CPA Core, in a Common or a Licensure version

  • CPA Core – Common builds financial reporting, assurance and trust, big data and analytics, and tax. CPA Core – Licensure contains all of Common plus more depth, and is required for anyone who wants a public accounting licence. N2W5ON1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Common: two to three cases of 60 to 120 minutes each, 3 hours in total. N1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Licensure: Part A is the same cases as the Common exam (3 hours); Part B is one 2-hour licensure case. Passing needs overall sufficiency and “readiness for licensure” on Part B. N1
  • A candidate who passes only Part A still progresses in the program; a separate licensure exam can be written after certification. N1
OntarioCommon 8 weeks (first online offering Jul 12, 2027); Licensure 14 weeks (first online offering May 31, 2027). ON2
QuebecThe licensure version is called “Core – Common + Public accountancy” and leads to the CPA auditor designation. Common 8 weeks + 2; Common + Public accountancy 14 weeks + 2. QC3QC1
WestLicensure first starts May 29, 2027, Common Jul 10, 2027; both lead to the Sep 16, 2027 exam. Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. W7W8
AtlanticSame start dates as the West (May 29 and Jul 10, 2027). Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. A2
Step 4 · Module 3

Module 3: CPA Leadership

  • Applies the decision process to real-world challenges that integrate every topic area; the focus is critical thinking and the CPA Ethical Mindset. N2
  • Professional Final Exam 2: one 5-hour comprehensive case of moderate complexity, with limited direction and designed to be time-pressured. This is the only disclosed exam in the program. N1
  • Heaviest content areas on the exam: Strategy, Risk Management and Innovation (20–35%), Ethical Decision-Making and Governance (15–30%), Management Decision-Making (15–30%). N1
Ontario10 weeks; first online offering Jun 28, 2027. Exam 1 may be written before or after this module. ON2ON13
Quebec10 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online. Each exam must be passed before moving to the next module. QC3QC2
WestFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Learners may take Leadership before writing Exam 1, but on a first attempt Exam 1 must be written before or together with Exam 2. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. W7W11W8
AtlanticFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. A2
Step 5 · Checkpoint

Checkpoint: experience must be finished before the last module

  • Every region requires all experience requirements to be met before a learner can register for CPA Professional Readiness. This is the main structural change from the current program. ON1W5A1QC2
  • 24 months of qualifying experience, net of leaves: up to 8 months of Foundational experience and at least 16 months of Professional experience. ON5W9A1QC6
  • In Ontario and the West, Professional experience needs a CPA mentor and an experience (work) plan approved by the provincial body before it starts to count. In Quebec a CPA mentor must accompany the candidate and approve the work plan, which the Order must then approve. ON5W11QC6QC1
OntarioFoundational experience can date from up to five years before Foundational Development; all 24 months can be Professional if the role is already at that level. Full-time is 35 hours a week. ON5ON12
QuebecExperience must be completed and recognized by the Order. Full-time is at least 32 hours a week; the Order checks only a work plan at the start and a report at the end. QC2QC6
WestExams 1 and 2 must also be passed. Full-time equivalent is 35 hours a week. Organizations can hold “pre-reviewed” experience plans. W11
AtlanticExams 1 and 2 and all practical experience must be complete before the module. CPA ASB approves the work plan. A1A7
Step 6 · Module 4

Module 4: CPA Professional Readiness

  • Self-study plus a five-day, in-person, case-based experience covering the code of conduct, teamwork, and emerging global, social and technological issues. W5ON1N2
  • Professional Final Exam 3: one 2-hour professional-judgment case and one 1-hour ethical decision-making case. Each case is marked holistically and both must be passed. Not designed to be time-pressured. N1
  • After passing Exam 3 the learner applies for membership in their province. W5A1
OntarioDelivered by CPA Ontario itself, five days in person. The first module “takes place in winter 2028”; first Exam 3 is Jan 20, 2028. No exemptions from this module. ON2ON4ON13
QuebecDelivered only by the Order, for both pathways: 5 days in person plus 2 weeks of online preparation. QC3QC5
WestFirst offering starts Dec 11, 2027 with the in-person workshop Dec 13–17, 2027; Exam 3 on Jan 20, 2028. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. W7W8
AtlanticSame first offering: starts Dec 11, 2027, workshop Dec 13–17, 2027. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. A2
Step 7 · Finish

Membership

  • The designation and its legal recognition do not change; graduates of the new program receive the same CPA designation. QC1
  • Public accounting licensure is applied for after membership and requires the Licensure version of CPA Core and Exam 1 plus the licensure experience. W11ON1
OntarioLicensure pathway: all 24 months in an External Audit Training Office, with at least 2,500 chargeable hours including 1,250 in assurance (625 audit). ON15ON5
QuebecCPA auditor: 24 months at an audit firm including 1,250 assurance hours, 625 of them auditing general-purpose financial statements. QC1
WestAudit: 1,250 chargeable assurance hours, at least 625 in audit. Review: 1,250, at least 625 in audit or review. Compilation: 625. W11
AtlanticLicensure experience needs a Licensed Public Accountant as mentor and an organization registered for public accounting with the provincial body; applicable chargeable hours are required to meet licensure requirements. A7

All modules
General statementsCPA Ontario states a weekly commitment of a minimum of 15 hours for the online option. For the in-person option it states full-time or structured part-time, depending on the institution. ON2 As of Nov 18, 2026, CPA Ontario's Choose Your Path page and its examination schedule page did not state an exam-preparation period between the end of a module and its examination. ON2ON4CPA Core, common path (program delivered by the Order): the Order gives a duration of 8 weeks. QC3 The Order's program page says each module is followed by 1 or 2 weeks of preparation for its examination, for information purposes only. QC2 CPA Core, common path (program delivered by the Order): the module content page states 2 weeks of exam preparation after the 8 weeks. QC3 The Order says the modules of its program will begin in May 2027. It gives no start date for individual modules. QC2As of Nov 18, 2026 (texts downloaded that day), CPAWSB's Module Information page, its Schedules page and its draft policies did not state a length in weeks for any module. The Schedules page gives a module start date and an exam date for each offering. W7W5 As of Nov 18, 2026, CPAWSB's Module Information page, Schedules page and draft policies did not state a separate exam-preparation period. The draft policies say only that the standard track aims for learners to arrive at the next available exam date. W11W7As of Nov 18, 2026, CPA Atlantic School of Business's CPA Professional Program page did not state a length in weeks for any module. Its module schedule gives a module start date and an exam date for each offering. A2 As of Nov 18, 2026, CPA Atlantic School of Business's CPA Professional Program page did not state a separate exam-preparation period. A2
Regular and flexible tracksCPA Ontario does not use the terms regular, standard, flexible or extended track. It describes two options, online and in-person. It calls the online option “Flexible — study on your own schedule” and the in-person option “Structured — fixed class schedules”. ON2The Order does not use the terms regular, standard or extended track. It calls the program it delivers a “flexible program” that can be taken on a part-time basis or on an accelerated basis, with modules and exams completed at the candidate's own pace. QC2CPAWSB says the program has two pacing tracks: a standard track, and a flexible track that allows module completion in about twice the time of the standard track. W5 CPAWSB gives the learning commitment as about 20 hours a week in the standard track and 10 hours a week in the flexible track. It says learners can switch tracks. ONFor the exemption, a transcript showing successful completion of degree-credit courses (or equivalent as determined by CPA Ontario) with course names that match the seven named courses is sufficient evidence of those seven. For the other eight, a transcript showing successful completion of eight degree-credit courses (or equivalent as determined by CPA Ontario) that the institution identifies as part of its business department offerings and/or as required for a business or commerce degree is sufficient evidence. ON12
ONCPA Ontario decides whether completed CPA Qualifying Courses have the required learning outcomes by reviewing the institution's description of the courses in their course outlines. ON12
ONCourses accepted by another Canadian CPA provincial or regional body for entry to the CPA Professional Program may be recognized by CPA Ontario toward meeting entry requirements. ON11
QCThe Order says the admission requirements currently in effect will remain for the new program, including successful completion of a bachelor's degree recognized by the Order, obtained within the five years preceding the admission application. QC1
QCTo register with the Order, a person must have completed a bachelor's degree recognized by the Order in Quebec or the equivalent, or be about to finish the last term of that degree or the equivalent and have finished all courses in time for the start of the CPA program, and must be ready to start the CPA program. QC15
QCThe new licensing regulation, which comes into force on January 1, 2027, makes it a condition for the CPA permit that the candidate holds a diploma recognized by regulation of the Office des professions du Québec, or has obtained a diploma or training equivalence under the Order's equivalence regulation, and provides proof of it. QC12
QCThirteen Quebec universities are recognized by the Order and the Quebec government as offering the required program. The Order says each program includes all the prerequisite courses for admission to the CPA Professional Education Program (PEP), and it gives a list of prerequisite courses for each university. A student must pass all the courses on that list before finishing the program; otherwise they must be passed before beginning the PEP. QC23
QCA minimum grade point average of 2.8 will no longer be required for the new program delivered by the Order. Universities offering the graduate option may still set their own minimum average. QC1
QCA person who does not hold one of the bachelor's degrees recognized by the Order, or the equivalent, must go through the equivalence process before starting the CPA Professional Program. QC1
QCThe Order says the key prerequisites for equivalency recognition (for example financial accounting, auditing and taxation courses) will be largely the same under the new program, and that new evaluation schedules or a standard schedule will be developed. QC1
WestIn the West, exemption from the Knowledge Assessment requires at least 45 credit hours in accounting or business courses, from post-secondary institutions, the CPA preparatory courses, or both. 21 credit hours must cover required topics and 24 credit hours may cover other accounting and business topic areas. W18W11
WestThe CPAWSB draft policies list six required topic areas for the 21 credit hours: Intermediate Financial Reporting; Advanced Financial Reporting; Management Accounting (introductory management accounting courses are not eligible); Finance; Assurance; and Taxation. W11
WestFor the other 24 credit hours, CPAWSB says any eligible accounting or business-related course completed at a recognized post-secondary institution may count. Courses must have credits awarded and recorded on the official transcript. Continuing education courses, work terms, co-op placements and other experiential placements are not eligible. W3
WestCPAWSB says most accounting and business-related courses offered by post-secondary institutions, excluding private vocational institutions (career colleges), are expected to meet the 24-credit-hour requirement. W18
WestAt least one course counted toward the 45 credit hours must have been completed within five years. The CPAWSB web pages measure this from the application for admission; the draft policies measure it from the start of the Foundational Development module. The date used is the course completion date on the official transcript. W2W11W3
WestPre-verified qualifying courses for the required topic areas are published by institution. CPABC publishes the list for British Columbia and Yukon colleges and universities, and says applicants do not need to complete all courses at the same institution. A person whose institution is not listed may still qualify. W3BC4
WestApplicants who complete all the courses in the CPA PEP Academic Prerequisites Guide by December 31, 2028 will be exempt from the Knowledge Assessment in the new program. W3
Atl.In the Atlantic region, exemption from the Knowledge Assessment requires a minimum of 45 credit hours in accounting or business courses from post-secondary institutions, the CPA preparatory courses, or both. A6
Atl.At least 21 of the 45 credit hours must cover six required topic areas: Intermediate Financial Reporting; Advanced Financial Reporting; Intermediate Management Accounting; Finance; Assurance; and Taxation (Canadian). Introductory management accounting courses do not count toward the 21 credit hours. A6
Atl.The remaining 24 credit hours may be any accounting or business-related courses from a post-secondary institution. CPA Atlantic publishes a list of course prefixes that count and says the list is not exhaustive. A6
Atl.At least one course among the 45 credit hours must have been completed within five years of admission, based on the completion date of the course on the transcript. A6
Atl.CPA Atlantic publishes pre-verified qualifying courses for the required topic areas by province. A person whose program is not listed may still be eligible for the exemption. A6
Transcript assessment
ONIn Ontario, CPA Ontario assesses transcripts. The transcript assessment determines whether the academic requirements are fulfilled and whether the applicant is exempt from the Knowledge Assessment. ON12ON9
ONApplicants and students request a transcript assessment in My Portal. It may be requested before applying for student registration, at the same time as the application, or when required to change registration category. ON12
ONFor courses or degrees completed in Canada, CPA Ontario requires official transcripts, sent directly to CPA Ontario through an approved education credential platform or, where the institution does not support electronic delivery, mailed in a sealed envelope from the institution's Registrar's Office. Transcripts sent by the applicant are not accepted as official. ON12ON26
ONFor courses or degrees completed outside Canada, CPA Ontario requires a course-by-course credential evaluation by World Education Services (WES) Canada through its International Credential Advantage Package (ICAP), sent directly to CPA Ontario by WES Canada, or an equivalent credential evaluation approved by CPA Ontario. ON12
ONThe CPA Ontario transcript assessment fee is $150 plus HST. Fees for official transcripts and for the WES report are set by the institution and by WES and are paid directly to them. ON26ON12
ONCPA Ontario says transcript assessments typically take up to eight weeks, counted from when all required documents have been received. A question-and-answer list on its Transcript Reassessment page gives up to six weeks for applicants educated in Canada and up to eight weeks for those educated outside Canada. ON26ON27
ONA transcript assessment result may only be submitted with an application within one year of the date the result was provided to the applicant. ON12
ONBefore student registration opens in January 2027, a person can apply for a transcript assessment for the new program by checking a box on the application. CPA Ontario says this assessment is primarily intended for people considering taking the education components online at an accredited post-secondary institution. ON26
ONCPA Ontario calculates the grade point average from the transcripts, based on 40 three-credit courses totalling 120 credit hours. If more than 120 credit hours were completed, the highest grades are used. ON9ON12
ONAn applicant or student who disagrees with a transcript assessment decision may escalate it to the SVP, Student Services, whose decision is final. A reassessment can be requested after completing new courses, to submit additional documents, or to have a result rechecked. ON12ON27
QCHolders of a recognized bachelor's degree attach their most recent official bachelor's transcript to the Order's registration form. If the final term's results are not yet on the transcript, admission is conditional until the final official transcript is sent. QC15
QCIf more than 99 credits were earned in the program, the Order's admissions team calculates a new cumulative grade point average on the courses that count toward registration. QC23
QCA person whose recognized bachelor's degree was obtained five or more years ago must open a file to have skills and knowledge assessed before beginning the program. For each CPA competency, at least one intermediate or advanced level course must have been completed within the past five years as of the admission date; otherwise an update may be required. QC26QC23
QCPeople trained in Canada or abroad who do not hold a recognized bachelor's degree apply to the Order under the "training equivalence" profile. The Order evaluates their studies against the recognized bachelor's programs and then gives them a list of prerequisite courses to pass. QC25QC24
QCA training equivalence file must include two pieces of identification, a copy of all degrees, a transcript for each degree, the official comparative evaluation of studies completed outside Quebec issued by the Quebec immigration ministry (MIFI) or by World Education Services (WES), and a curriculum vitae. Proof of membership in an accounting organization can be added where applicable. QC25
QCThe Order's equivalence fees are $65.54 for opening the file and $193.16 for reviewing it. Reviewing an additional course list or updating the file costs $65.54. QC25
QCThe Order says to allow 90 days for processing an equivalence file, counted from the date the file is complete and compliant, and notes that processing times may be longer than usual because of a high volume of applications. The new licensing regulation, for an equivalence of the permit conditions on the professional training program, the internship and the examinations, requires the Order to give its reasoned written decision within 90 days of receiving the complete file or, where applicable, of the completion of the measures it required. QC27QC25QC12
QCThe Order's list of prerequisite courses is valid for two years. After that a new analysis is needed. The list is approved by the Qualification committee, which generally meets once a month. QC27QC25
QCIn reviewing an equivalence file the Order considers university degrees, the credits earned, the nature and content of the courses, academic background, professional experience, how recent the studies and experience are, and changes in Canadian standards since then. QC25
QCThe Order's equivalence FAQ says the first condition to begin the process is an undergraduate degree with a minimum of 90 credits or the equivalent. As of Nov 18, 2026 the equivalence website still described these steps as leading to the CPA Professional Education Program and carried a notice that a new professional program is coming in 2027. QC27QC24
QCAn applicant who disagrees with the Order's equivalence decision can submit comments in writing within 30 days of receiving it; the file then goes to the Qualification committee. QC25
QCCurrent program: the Order's administrative procedures (last amended October 2024) require, in order to register as a candidate, an official transcript showing the date the diploma was obtained or a document the Order judges equivalent. QC28
WestIn the West the transcript check for the new program is called an Academic Review. CPAWSB's draft policies (published May 2026) say CPAWSB completes it and it must be done before an admission application can be submitted. CPAWSB's Knowledge Assessment page says a completed Academic Review is required to write the Knowledge Assessment. W11W4
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (published May 2026) say an official transcript and/or official documents are required for an Academic Review. Where an official transcript is not yet available, an unofficial transcript can start the review, but official transcripts are needed to finalize it without conditions. W11
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (published May 2026) say an Academic Review is valid from the date it is issued until one year from issue or the expiry of any official documents, whichever is earlier. Additional coursework completed within that period can be submitted for review at no additional cost. An expired review cannot be reactivated or amended; a new request and fee are required. W11
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (published May 2026) say an Academic Review has one of three results: Academically Eligible, Academically Eligible with Conditions, or Not Academically Eligible. W11
WestThe CPAWSB fee schedule for academic year 2027-2028 lists the Academic Review fee (non-refundable) as $150 for Domestic and $200 for International and Advanced Experience. All fees are subject to GST. W8
WestAs of the CPAWSB admission requirements page updated May 15, 2026, the Academic Review process was not yet available and applicants were asked not to submit an application yet. W2
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (published May 2026) say international degree holders must prove Canadian degree equivalency through an evaluation by a recognized third-party credential assessment service. W11
WestCurrent program: a CPAWSB transcript assessment decides eligibility for CPA PEP and shows which prerequisite courses are outstanding. It is valid for one year from the date it is completed, and can be updated at no additional fee before it expires. W35W39
WestCurrent program: the CPAWSB transcript assessment fee (non-refundable) is $150 + GST for a Canadian degree and $200 + GST for an international degree, Mature status, IFAC members and MOU members. W31
WestCurrent program: CPAWSB accepts official documents sent directly by the issuing institution, digitally or by mail in a sealed envelope. For Canadian degree holders the typical processing time is 10 business days after all documents are received; for Mature Status applicants it is 20 business days. W40W38W37
Atl.CPA Atlantic School of Business charges an eligibility assessment fee of $150 plus HST (non-refundable) for transcripts from institutions inside Canada and the United States, and $200 plus HST for transcripts for transcripts the page treats as international. These fees are listed with the 2027 fee information for the CPA Professional Program. A2
Atl.An official transcript, requested from the applicant's post-secondary institution, is required. CPA Atlantic says it may take up to 8 weeks to process an application. A11
Atl.Applicants with a degree that the page treats as international must submit a third-party assessment of the degree; a World Education Services (WES) International Credential Advantage Package (ICAP) is required. Detailed course syllabi may also be required. A15
Atl.To apply, a person first contacts a CPA Atlantic advisor; once eligibility is confirmed through the advisor consultation, access to the application is provided. A16
Experience pathway (no degree)
ONOntario's Regulation 9-3 has a Non-Degree registration category for an applicant who may not have a degree and who has at least eight years of relevant accounting or business experience satisfactory to the Registrar, and who provides two letters of reference satisfactory to the Registrar. ON13
ONA Non-Degree applicant in Ontario must submit a completed work experience assessment form showing the eight years. The Registrar assesses it on the basis of employment in a role or roles that fall within at least one of the CPA Training Areas. ON12
ONOnce the Registrar approves the work experience, the Ontario Non-Degree applicant submits a student application with two letters of reference dated within three months, from people who have known the applicant for at least three years: one from a member in good standing of CPA Ontario or another provincial or territorial body, and one from a contact at a current employer. ON12
ONCurrent program: CPA Ontario's Mature category is for applicants with at least eight years of relevant accounting or business experience with proficiency in two Level 1 competency areas. A post-secondary degree is not needed to register under it. ON28
QCThe Order's equivalence website says that a foreign-trained professional with more than 8 years of in-depth, wide-ranging accounting experience may be offered a prior learning and professional experience recognition process, for which fees apply. QC25
QCUnder the new licensing regulation, relevant work experience (the nature of the work, the complexity and responsibility level of the assignments, and its length) is one of the factors taken into account when the Order assesses an equivalence of the permit conditions on the professional training program, the internship and the examinations. QC12
WestCPAWSB's draft policies call it the "Alternate Pathway: Advanced Experience". Applicants who do not meet the degree requirement may request an assessment based on extensive relevant experience. It is an alternative to the degree, the 120 credit hours of post-secondary education and the minimum GPA requirements. W11
WestThe draft policies say applicants who meet the degree requirement are not eligible to choose the Advanced Experience pathway. All other admission requirements continue to apply, and applicants must still demonstrate the required accounting and business knowledge or pass the Knowledge Assessment. W11
WestThe draft policies say an Advanced Experience applicant must demonstrate a minimum of eight years of relevant, paid experience in one or more CPA specific competency topic areas, provide employer validation of that experience, and provide a character reference. W11
WestCPAWSB's applicant-type page describes the Advanced Experience Pathway as possibly available to a person with no degree or professional designation who has at least eight years of relevant paid accounting experience. W36
WestCurrent program: CPAWSB's Mature Status route is for applicants without a degree who have at least eight years of accounting- and business-relevant, full-time work experience. If approved, it may exempt them from the degree and 120-credit-hour requirements for CPA PEP; all 14 prerequisite courses are still required. W27W37
Atl.CPA Atlantic calls it a "Degree Waiver". Applicants without a degree can request an assessment to waive the degree requirement if they have a minimum of eight years of practical experience in any two of the CPA technical competency areas and have achieved at least Level 1 proficiency in these areas. A9
Atl.A Non-Degree Holder entrant in the Atlantic region must also provide an evaluation form sent directly from the employer and a personal character reference, and must successfully complete the accounting coursework requirements. A9
Atl.Current program: CPA Atlantic's "Workforce Applicants" without an undergraduate degree could qualify for CPA PEP with at least eight years of relevant experience in the CPA technical competency areas, plus prerequisite subject coverage. A15

blocks.cards:
Ontario

CPA Ontario
  • Universities teach the first three modules and set their fees. Online through Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey Executive Education, or in person in an accredited graduate program. ON2ON12
  • 70% GPA across the required 120 credit hours; entry-level knowledge (the final qualifying course, or the Knowledge Assessment) must be completed within three years before enrolling in Foundational Development. ON9
  • Transition is automatic. CPA Ontario moves students across on fixed cut-off dates from July 15, 2027; registration by Dec 31, 2026 is needed to stay on the current CFE route. ON14ON6
  • Regulations in effect, fees not yet shared. Regulations 9-3 and 9-4 took effect Nov 1, 2026; CPA Ontario says fees for the examinations and modules “will be shared when available”. ON13ON14ON4

Quebec

Ordre des CPA du Québec
  • Two pathways: the Order’s online program or a graduate program at one of 11 universities; both end with the Order’s Professional Readiness module. QC2QC5
  • No minimum average for the Order’s program; the degree must be recent (five years). QC1
  • Strictly sequential: pass each exam before the next module. The Module 1 exam is run by the universities for their own students. QC2QC1
  • Practical experience was already 24 months in Quebec; what changes is the Foundational / Professional split and lighter monitoring. QC9QC6

West and the territories

CPAWSB with CPABC, CPA Alberta, CPA Saskatchewan, CPA Manitoba, CPA Yukon, CPA NWT/Nunavut
  • Most complete rulebook so far: full fee schedule, dated module and exam calendar to September 2028, and published policies. W8W7W11
  • Standard or flexible pace (about 20 or 10 hours a week), with a two-day in-person orientation. W5W11
  • 65% GPA on the last 60 credits; eight-year experience route for applicants without a degree. W11
  • Up to two extra years on transition. One set of policies covers all four provinces and the territories. W12W11

Atlantic

CPA Atlantic School of Business with CPA NS, NB, NL and PEI
  • Same calendar and module fees as the West; first modules May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. A2
  • Only region with an official total: about $16,800 + HST for the program over 2.5 years, including a $500 one-time registration fee. A2
  • The school approves work plans: a Professional work plan must be approved by the mentor and CPA ASB, and CPA ASB reviews experience before a transition. Under the transition policy, the transition application itself is approved by the relevant Atlantic provincial body. A7A4
  • Up to three extra years on transition; preparatory course registration closes Oct 20, 2027. A3A1

BC learners without one are told to contact CPABC. ON16ON4[OPEN – fees for the Order’s program not yet set; no changes to dues anticipated]Academic review $150 (international $200); application $150; annual dues $1,200; technology fee $350. Not eligible: those who complete the current program on or before Dec 31, 2028; those awaiting a third CFE result after two unsuccessful attempts; and those eligible for deregistration under listed sections of Regulation 9-1 on or before Dec 31, 2028. ON14ON6Candidates stay in the current program until it is no longer offered at their university or by the Order; transition only then. QC1QC7Time limit after Dec 31, 2028 and good standing. MOU candidates are excluded. W12W15Same national framework: time limit after Dec 31, 2028 and good standing. A4How it happensCPA Ontario transitions students itself on fixed dates once a component can no longer be finished: Jul 15, 2027 (Core 1), Oct 15, 2027 (Core 2), Apr 15, 2028 (electives), Jul 15, 2028 (Capstone 1), Sep 7, 2028 (Capstone 2), Dec 31, 2028 (the rest). ON14A personal transition plan confirmed with the Order. QC7By application during the window; approved by the provincial body; final once processed. W12By application, not automatic. The transition policy says a transition is not confirmed until approved by the Atlantic provincial body; the FAQ page says CPA Atlantic School of Business reviews and approves the application. A4A3Extra time after transitionUp to three years, to a maximum of seven, applied on Jan 1, 2029; not for students who transition into the Pre-Certification or Interim categories. ON14ON6Three years added, to a maximum of seven. QC1Up to two years, to a maximum of seven. W12Up to three years, to a maximum of seven. A3A5Legacy preparatory coursesLast PREP exam December 2026. ON14ON6[OPEN – the Order’s academic prerequisites page says each recognized bachelor’s program includes all the…]Offered until December 2027; last registration Nov 4, 2027. blocks.fd-glance:
Region
66 of 66
RegionWhat the source says
Four modules, taken in order
AllThe national Module Guide says the program consists of the Foundational Development module and three professional modules: CPA Core, CPA Leadership and CPA Professional Readiness. It says the CPA Leadership module follows CPA Core. N2
ONCPA Ontario’s Regulation 9-3 says the education component is four sequential modules, in this order: Foundational Development, CPA Core (common path or licensure path), CPA Leadership and CPA Professional Readiness. ON13
QCThe Quebec Order’s regulation requires a candidate to pass four parts (“volets”) of professional education, and each part is open only to a candidate who has passed the one before. The Order’s program page says each module must be completed in order and its exam passed before the next module. QC12QC2
WestCPAWSB says the program consists of four modules, completed in sequence: Foundational Development, CPA Core, CPA Leadership and CPA Professional Readiness. W5W16W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic School of Business says the program consists of four modules, completed in sequence. A2A3
Entry by coursework or the Knowledge Assessment
AllThe national Module Guide says learners who have obtained the specified accounting and business knowledge at a post-secondary institution are exempt from the Knowledge Assessment, and all other learners must pass it to enter the Foundational Development module. The Exam Guide calls it an optional entrance exam. N2N1
ONCPA Ontario says there are two ways to show entry-level knowledge: completing the CPA Qualifying Courses at a post-secondary institution or passing the Knowledge Assessment. Regulation 9-3 requires the Knowledge Assessment unless the student has completed the CPA Qualifying Courses, the last within the last three years, or is a member of an accounting body outside Canada. ON9ON13
QCThe Quebec Order says a person who does not hold one of the bachelor’s degrees recognized by the Order, or the equivalent, must go through the equivalence process before starting the program. As of Nov 18, 2026 the Order’s new-program pages did not mention a Knowledge Assessment. QC1QC12
WestCPAWSB says applicants show accounting and business knowledge in one of two ways: write and pass the Knowledge Assessment, or qualify for an exemption from it through eligible accounting and business coursework (45 credit hours). W2W16W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic says accounting and business knowledge can be shown either by completing 45 credit hours in accounting and business or by passing the Knowledge Assessment. Applicants must write the Knowledge Assessment before the Foundational Development module unless they qualify for an exemption through post-secondary coursework. A2A3
Provincial rules take precedence
WestThe Western Region policies say the CPA profession strives for national consistency, but provincial regulations and bylaws take precedence over national requirements, and learners must refer to the regulations of each relevant provincial body. W11
Four exams: one module exam and three Professional Final Exams
AllThe national Exam Guide sets out the Foundational Development Exam, CPA Core (Professional Final Exam 1, in a Common and a Licensure version), CPA Leadership (Professional Final Exam 2) and CPA Professional Readiness (Professional Final Exam 3). N1
ONCPA Ontario’s Regulation 9-3 says the examination component is four examinations, in this order: the Foundational Development Examination, then Professional Final Examination 1A (common path) or 1B (licensure), Professional Final Examination 2 and Professional Final Examination 3. ON13
QCThe Quebec Order says there is an exam for the Foundational Development module, and the three parts of the Professional Final Exam are offered at the end of the CPA Core, CPA Leadership and CPA Professional Readiness modules. QC1
WestCPAWSB says the program includes three Professional Final Exams and one module exam. The Western Region policies list four module levels and four associated exams. W6W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic says learners must pass the Foundational Development Exam before moving on to CPA Core, and that each part of the three-part Professional Final Exam can be written immediately after passing the associated module. A2
Exam hours: 16 on the Common path, 18 on the Licensure path
AllThe national Exam Guide gives five hours for the Foundational Development Exam, three hours for CPA Core – Common or five hours for CPA Core – Licensure, five hours for CPA Leadership and three hours for CPA Professional Readiness. Our sum: 16 hours on the Common path and 18 hours on the Licensure path. N1
ONCPA Ontario’s examinations page gives the formats: CPA Core – Common totals three hours; CPA Core – Licensure is a three-hour Part A plus a two-hour Part B; CPA Leadership is one five-hour case; CPA Professional Readiness is a two-hour case and a one-hour case. ON3
QCThe Quebec Order’s exam calendar gives a duration of 5 h for the Foundational exam, 3 h for Professional final exam part 1, 3 h (Part A) plus 2 h (Part B) for the public accountancy version of part 1, 5 h for part 2 and 3 h for part 3. Our sum: 16 hours without the public accountancy version and 18 hours with it. QC4
WestCPAWSB’s examinations page gives the formats: Professional Final Exam 1 (Common) totals three hours; the Licensure version is a three-hour Part A plus a two-hour Part B; Professional Final Exam 2 is one five-hour case; Professional Final Exam 3 is a two-hour case and a one-hour case. W6
Months of experience
ONCPA Ontario requires a minimum of 24 months of experience, net of absences: up to 8 months of Foundational Work Experience and at least 16 months of Professional Work Experience. ON5ON13
QCThe Quebec Order requires 24 months of practical experience recognized by the Order. Its regulation sets the practical training at 24 months full time. QC6QC12
WestIn the West, a minimum of 24 months of full-time qualifying experience, excluding leave, is required: up to 8 months of Foundational experience and at least 16 months of Professional experience. W9W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic requires a minimum of 24 months of qualifying experience, excluding time away from work: up to 8 months of Foundational Experience and at least 16 months of Professional Experience. A7A1
Experience complete before the last module; last exam after the experience
AllThe national Module Guide says learners must meet all practical experience requirements before they take the CPA Professional Readiness module. N2
ONCPA Ontario says all experience requirements must be complete before enrolling in the final module, CPA Professional Readiness, which culminates in Professional Final Exam III. Regulation 9-3 places Professional Final Examination 2 before completion of the work experience and Professional Final Examination 3 after it. ON1ON13
QCThe Quebec Order says the practical experience must be completed and recognized by the Order before a candidate may take the Professional Readiness module and Part 3 of the Professional Final Exam. QC6QC2QC12
WestCPAWSB says a learner must have met all experience requirements and passed Professional Final Exams 1 and 2 before registering for the CPA Professional Readiness module. Professional Final Exam 3 is written after passing that module. W5W11W16
Atl.CPA Atlantic says learners must meet all experience requirements before starting the Professional Readiness module. Professional Final Exam Part 3 is written after passing that module. A1A7A2
Exam sittings three times a year: January, May, September
ONCPA Ontario offers the program’s examinations and the Professional Readiness module up to three times per year. Its schedule lists the Foundational Development Examination and Professional Final Examinations 1 and 2 in September 2027, January 2028, May 2028, September 2028 and January 2029, and Professional Final Examination 3 from January 2028. It also lists a Knowledge Assessment sitting on March 23, 2027. ON4
QCThe Quebec Order says the three parts of the Professional Final Exam, and the Foundational Development exam for the program delivered by the Order, will be taken at an exam centre in Montréal in September, January and May. Exams will be offered in centres outside Montréal at least once per year. QC1
WestCPAWSB says that after the first offering in September 2027, the Professional Final Exams will be offered three times annually, with timing to be confirmed. Its exam schedule lists sittings in September 2027, January 2028, May 2028 and September 2028. W13W7
Atl.CPA Atlantic says that starting in September 2027, all exams in the new program will be offered annually in January, May and September. A3
Seven year maximum
ONIn Ontario, students have a maximum of 7 years from the CPAPP Commencement Date to complete the program. That date is the first date a student attends their first required module or examination. ON13
QCIn Quebec, the regulation gives a candidate 7 years from the date of registration with the Order to meet the program, practical experience and exam conditions, with a possible extension of up to two years for a serious reason. For candidates who transition, the Order says the maximum time allotted will be seven years in total. QC12QC1
WestIn the West, learners must complete all education, examination and experience within a time limit of up to seven years, which starts at the start of the Foundational Development module. W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic’s transition policy says candidates who transition may receive up to three additional years, but the total time limit in the new program cannot exceed seven years from the date of admission into the new program. A5A4
The three day CFE is replaced by three Professional Final Exams
ONCPA Ontario’s regulations define the CPA Professional Program as the program that runs alongside the legacy program from January 1, 2027 and replaces it after December 31, 2028. A student who transitions before passing the CFE must, at a minimum, complete the Professional Readiness module and Professional Final Exam III. ON15ON6
QCThe Quebec Order says the three parts of the Professional Final Exam will replace the current module exams and the Common Final Examination (CFE), and there will no longer be a consecutive three-day exam. Each part is offered at the end of its module. QC1
WestCPAWSB’s program comparison shows the certification exam as a 3-day CFE following the final module in the current program, and as 3 CPA Professional Final Exams, written following the associated module, in the new program. Each part can be written immediately after passing the associated module. W16W5
Atl.CPA Atlantic says that instead of waiting until the end of the program to assess competency through a multi-day exam, exams are tested after each module, and each part of the three-part Professional Final Exam can be written immediately after passing the associated module. A2A3
CPA Core has two pathways: Common and Licensure
AllThe national Module Guide says all learners choose either the CPA Core – Common or the CPA Core – Licensure module, and that CPA Core – Licensure is for learners who are considering a public accounting licence. N2
ONCPA Ontario says students select one of two pathways in the CPA Core module, Common or Licensure. Those seeking licensure must pass the Licensure version of CPA Core and the Licensure version of PFE 1. ON1ON13
QCIn Quebec the two paths of the Core module are called Common and Common + Public Accountancy. Candidates who want a public accountancy permit must choose the CPA Core – Common + Public accountancy module and pass the public accounting version of Professional Final Exam, part 1. QC1QC3
WestCPAWSB says learners choose between two versions of the CPA Core module, Common and Licensure. Those who intend to pursue a career in public accounting must complete the Licensure version. W5W11
Atl.CPA Atlantic says learners choose between two versions of the CPA Core module, Common and Licensure. Those who intend to pursue a career in public accounting must complete the Licensure version. A2
Current program ends Dec 31, 2028; final CFE September 2028
ONIn Ontario, students in the legacy program have until December 31, 2028 to complete it or transition. The regulation gives September 2028 as the end date for the Common Final Examination. ON14ON6
QCThe Quebec Order refers to the end of the current program on December 31, 2028, and to the last-ever CFE in September 2028. The regulation keeps the old rules for candidates registered before January 1, 2027 until the earlier of the date the old program and exam cease to be offered by the Order and December 31, 2028. QC1QC12
WestCPAWSB says candidates in CPA PEP have until December 31, 2028 to complete their current program, and the last CFE offering is in September 2028. W13W14
Atl.CPA Atlantic says candidates unable to complete CPA PEP by December 31, 2028 will be required to transition, and the last CFE offering will take place in September 2028. A1A3
Date 1: January 2027 (launch, registration, transition period opens)
ONCPA Ontario says the new program will launch in January 2027. Its regulation says the program begins to run alongside the legacy program on January 1, 2027. The 24-month transition period runs from January 2027 to December 2028. ON1ON15ON6
QCFor the program offered by the Quebec Order, registration will begin in January 2027. Some universities will offer the new program in January 2027 and others from May or September 2027. The new regulation comes into force on January 1, 2027. QC1QC12
WestCPAWSB says registration for the new program will open in early 2027, and refers to the program launching in January 2027. Transition is available only from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028. CPABC says the new program launches in May 2027. W1W13BC1
Atl.CPA Atlantic says the program launches in early 2027. The transition period is January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028. A1A3
Date 2: May 2027 (first modules start)
ONIn Ontario the first online module offerings begin in 2027: Foundational Development and CPA Core – Licensure on May 31, 2027, CPA Leadership on June 28, 2027 and CPA Core – Common on July 12, 2027. ON2
QCFor the program delivered by the Quebec Order, modules will begin in May 2027. QC2QC1
WestIn the West the first offering of new program modules is in May 2027; the schedule shows a module start date of May 15, 2027. W13W7
Atl.CPA Atlantic’s schedule shows the first module offering, May 2027 to September 2027, starting on May 15, 2027. A2
Date 3: September 15–16, 2027 (first exams)
ONCPA Ontario’s schedule shows the first Foundational Development and Professional Final Examination 2 sittings on September 15, 2027, and the first Professional Final Examination 1 sitting on September 16, 2027. The first Professional Final Examination 3 sitting is January 20, 2028. ON4
QCThe Quebec Order’s exam calendar shows, for September 2027, the Foundational exam and Professional final exam part 2 on September 15 and Professional final exam part 1 on September 16. Part 3 is marked N/A for September 2027 and first appears on January 20 in the January 2028 column. QC4
WestCPAWSB’s exam schedule shows the first sittings in September 2027, on September 15 and September 16, 2027. Its key dates list September 2027 as the first offering of the CPA Professional Final Exams. W7W13
Atl.CPA Atlantic’s schedule shows exam dates of September 15, 2027 and September 16, 2027 for the first module offerings. It says all exams in the new program will be offered starting in September 2027. A2A3
Date 4: December 31, 2028 (transition window closes)
ONCPA Ontario says eligible candidates must transition to the new program by December 2028. The regulation gives students until December 31, 2028 to complete the legacy program or transition. ON6ON14
QCIn the national-program section of its transition page, the Quebec Order says candidates who cannot finish before December 31, 2028 will be transferred to the new program. A candidate whose allowed period ends after December 31, 2028 and who has not finished by then must transition. QC7QC1
WestIn the West, transition is available only from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028, and December 2028 is the transition deadline for all learners and the end of CPA PEP. W13W14
Atl.CPA Atlantic says the transition period ends December 31, 2028 and everyone must transition by December 2028. A3A7

blocks.paths:
In-person graduate program in the summer, then a firm

The Ontario diploma model. A 12 or 13-week accredited diploma satisfies Foundational Development, CPA Core and CPA Leadership. Its graduates are exempt from CPA Ontario’s Foundational Development exam (the university may be approved to deliver its own) and can write Exams 1 and 2 as early as September of the same year. The timeline then shows full-time work, and the five-day Professional Readiness module once the minimum 24 months of work experience are complete. ON13U4U8ON1

If up to eight months of earlier co-op counts as Foundational experience, the 24 months finish sooner and Exam 3 moves up one or two sittings. Not every program follows this shape: Guelph’s master’s places Exam 1 in September and Exam 2 in January. ON5U1U26

Modules part time while working

The route with no graduate program: through the regional school in the West and Atlantic, online through a partner university in Ontario, or through the Order in Quebec. Each module is followed by its exam. W7A2ON2QC2

Dates follow the western regular-track calendar. In Ontario the three modules on this route are delivered online by a university rather than by the CPA body. W7ON2 The work bar is our arithmetic: 24 months of full-time qualifying experience counted from the start of Foundational Development. Under the western policies, Professional experience can accumulate once the learner is enrolled in that module, has a mentor and has an approved experience plan. W9W11

University graduate program in Quebec

HEC Montréal’s published sequence: courses in summer and fall, Exam 1 in January, a winter work term, CPA Leadership the next summer and Exam 2 in September. Professional Readiness and Exam 3 follow with the Order once the practical experience, which lasts a minimum of 24 months, is complete. QC13QC3QC6

Master’s over two summers (West)

The University of Saskatchewan’s published pathway: year 1 courses then Exam 1, year 2 courses then Exam 2, work in between, and Professional Readiness with Exam 3 at the end. CPAWSB’s FAQ says students in the two accredited programs will receive advanced placement and that more information “will be available soon”. U34U35W18 The two work bars add up to the minimum of 24 months of full-time qualifying experience on CPAWSB’s experience page (our arithmetic). W9
blocks.pathsNote: Illustrations only. Exam sittings follow the published September, January and May pattern. The end of each work bar, and the placing of Professional Readiness at the first offering after the 24 months are complete, are our arithmetic. W7ON4A3W18

ON30The candidate must meet at least one of Financial Reporting or Management Accounting, each met by completing two of its four task statements. All students meet their mentor at least twice a year and report in PERT. ON25ON25A pre-approved program, the experience verification route, or a combination. The experience verification route does not qualify for a public accountancy permit. The candidate writes two reports for each 12 months worked and has two mentor meetings a year. QC32QC32The Experience Verification Route lets the candidate choose the employer but requires more reporting in PERT; pre-approved programs are approved in advance. Audit and review experience can be gained only through pre-approved programs. Candidates meet their CPA mentor at least semi-annually. W24W24In the Pre-Approved Program Route the mentor is assigned through the employer; in the Experience Verification Route CPA Atlantic assesses and approves the position and the candidate finds their own mentor.
