RegionWhat the source says
New program: what experience must contain
ONUnless the Regulations specify otherwise, CPA Ontario's Regulation 9-3 requires every student to complete 24 months of work experience, not counting absences. This may be made up of up to 8 months of full-time Foundational Work Experience, at the discretion of the Director of Employer Relations, and at least 16 months of full-time Professional Work Experience. ON13
ONFoundational Work Experience is optional in Ontario. All 24 months may be Professional Work Experience if the student chooses. ON12
ONCPA Ontario's policies define a full-time position as one requiring 35 hours or more of work per week on a regular basis. Part-time experience is pro-rated against a full-time equivalent of 35 hours. ON12
ONAbsences in Ontario include vacation, sickness, study leave, professional development, CPA module and examination days, and personal leave. Statutory holidays, weekends and a reasonable amount of on-the-job training are not absences. ON12
ONThe student's role must fall within at least one of eight CPA Training Areas: Financial Reporting, Management Accounting, Assurance & Trust, Finance, Taxation, Strategy or Governance, Non-financial reporting, and Data (includes Big Data). ON12
ONFoundational Work Experience in Ontario has three Task Statements, each at proficiency level 2: F1, prepare or explain information for input into internal or external reporting; F2, identify the users' needs and prepare practical alternatives or variance analysis; F3, explain the analysis and findings in a transparent, understandable and professional manner. ON12ON30
ONTo count as Foundational Work Experience in Ontario, experience must have been obtained within the 5 years before the first day of the Foundational Development module and for at least three consecutive months. Students in the Member of Accounting Body Outside Canada and Member of Accounting Body Outside Canada – MOU registration categories are excepted from this rule. Foundational Work Experience must also require the application of judgment and cannot be clerical. ON13ON12
ONIn Ontario, work experience obtained before registration with CPA Ontario is considered only toward Foundational Work Experience, with the exception of provincial transfers. Experience gained before enrolling in the Foundational Development module is not recognized as Professional Work Experience unless Schedule E or F of the regulation provides otherwise. ON13
ONFor Professional Work Experience, an Ontario student chooses one learning outcome category, Financial Reporting or Management Accounting, and must master any two of its four Task Statements. The three Decision Competencies (Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication) are mandatory for everyone. ON30
ONCPA Ontario says the student must reach the highest proficiency level available in each Professional category, which is level 4 or 5 depending on the learning outcome. Its Task Statements page shows level 5 for the Financial Reporting, Management Accounting, Assurance & Trust, Professional Skepticism and Ethical Decision Making statements and level 4 for Communication. ON30ON12
ONOntario's four Financial Reporting Task Statements are: FR1, assess decision makers' needs and design reporting requirements or financial-reporting systems for external users; FR2, critically evaluate and reach a preliminary conclusion on three distinct GAAP transactions; FR3, prepare and critically evaluate financial statements and notes over two business periods; FR4, assess year-over-year variance analyses and interpret the root causes. For FR3 and FR4 at least one of the two periods must be a year end. ON12
ONOntario's four Management Accounting Task Statements are: MA1, assess decision makers' needs and critically evaluate information data systems for management reporting; MA2, create a forecast or budget with multiple and changing input variables across more than two business cycles; MA3, critically evaluate cost, revenue or profitability management for at least two business quarters; MA4, interpret variance analyses with explanations or recommendations over two business periods, at least one a year end. ON12
ONIn Ontario, experience obtained for less than three consecutive months may count toward the duration of Professional Work Experience. It is not considered when assessing whether the Task Statements have been met. ON12
ONFor the licensure pathway in Ontario, the CPA Training Areas must be Financial Reporting and Assurance & Trust, and all 24 months must be obtained in an External Audit Training Office. The CPA Mentor must hold a valid and current Public Accounting Licence, or be a member of a PTB who holds a valid and equivalent licence, certificate or other authorization to practise public accounting granted by that PTB. ON5ON13
ONOntario's Regulation 17-1 sets the new program's licensure experience at 24 months in an External Audit Training Office with a minimum of 2,500 chargeable hours. These include 1,250 chargeable hours in assurance services, of which at least 625 are in the audit of historical financial information and 100 are review procedures, plus 1,250 eligible hours in public accounting or designated services. ON15
ONOntario students on the licensure pathway must also meet the Assurance & Trust Task Statement AT1 at proficiency level 5. Through multiple external assurance engagements, they must plan and assess risk, design planned procedures, and critically evaluate supporting information to draw conclusions. ON12
ONOntario's Regulation 17-1 requires the licensure hours and competencies to be completed not more than five years before the licensure work experience completion date. If the licensure requirements are not met, the experience may still count toward membership, without eligibility for a Public Accounting Licence on admission. ON15ON12
ONIn Ontario, self-employment, unpaid work and experience obtained in academia are not eligible work experience. ON12
QCQuebec's regulation for the new program sets the professional training period (stage) at one or more periods of practical training totalling 24 months full time. The Order's website describes the practical experience as paid and lasting a minimum of 24 months. QC12QC6
QCIn Quebec up to 8 months may be recognized as foundational work experience, which is not mandatory. At least 16 months must be professional work experience, and all 24 months may be professional. QC6
QCIn Quebec, professional work experience can be acquired only after registering with the Order. Experience completed before registration can be recognized only as foundational work experience. QC6
QCTo be recognized in Quebec, experience acquired before registration must have been acquired after earning at least 30 university credits and in the last five years. It must be reported in the work plan and approved by a CPA in good standing at the same organization. QC6
QCIn Quebec, full time means a minimum of 32 hours per week and part time a minimum of 17.5 hours per week. Part-time experience is prorated on a 32-hour work week. QC6
QCThe Order lists eight training areas: Financial Reporting, Management Accounting, Assurance & Trust, Finance, Taxation, Strategy or Governance, Non-Financial Reporting and Big Data. In each, the role must not be limited to pulling data. QC6
QCThe Order organizes the practical experience competencies into six categories, each with task statements tied to a proficiency level from one to five. It says the proficiency level itself is not assessed, but rather the ability to complete the task in the statement. QC29
QCIn Quebec, up to 8 months can be recognized as foundational work experience if it allows the candidate to carry out three tasks: prepare or explain information for internal or external reporting, identify the user's needs and prepare practical alternatives or variance analyses, and explain analyses and findings in a transparent, understandable and professional manner. QC29
QCFor the CPA designation in Quebec, the candidate must meet the requirements of at least one of Financial Reporting or Management Accounting, plus the broad competency requirements. Each of those two categories is met by completing two of its four task statements. QC29
QCIn Quebec, the Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication categories each require all their task statements. A task statement counts as completed only when the candidate can answer "Yes" to every question the Order attaches to it. QC29
QCFor the CPA auditor designation under Quebec's new program, the 24 months must be completed at an audit firm and include 1,250 hours providing assurance on historical financial information. Of these, 625 hours must be in audit of general-purpose financial statements for different types of clients in various industries. QC30
QCFor the Quebec auditor path, the CPA mentor must hold a public accountancy permit, and the experience must let the candidate achieve learning objectives in financial reporting and assurance. The Order's grid has an Assurance & Trust category that is met by completing all its task statements. To receive the permit when the CPA permit is issued, the firm must be accredited by the Order as a public accountancy training environment. QC30QC29
QCIn Quebec, the practical experience must be completed and recognized by the Order before the candidate may take the Professional Readiness module and Part 3 of the Professional Final Exam. QC6
WestIn the West the new experience requirements take effect January 1, 2027. They apply to learners registering on or after that date and to those who transition after it. W9
WestCPAWSB's draft policies require a minimum of 24 months of full-time qualifying experience, exclusive of leave days. No more than 8 months may be Foundational Experience and at least 16 months must be Professional Experience. W11
WestThe Western draft policies define full-time work as a position requiring 35 hours or more per week on a regular basis. Working more than 35 hours does not shorten the duration, part-time work is prorated against 35 hours, and a position must amount to at least three full-time months to be recognized. W11
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026) define leave days as time away from work, including vacation, sickness, study leave, personal, parental and medical leave and professional development courses. Statutory holidays and a reasonable amount of on-the-job training are not leave days. W11
WestThe Western draft policies list ten CPA Training Areas: Financial Reporting; Management Decision-making and Information Systems/Technology; Assurance and Trust; Finance; Tax; Strategy, Risk Management and Innovation; Non-financial Reporting; Big Data and Data Analytics; Value Creation; and Ethical Decision-Making and Organizational Governance/Data Governance. W11
WestUnder CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026), learners may work in several CPA Training Areas, but their experience must support Level 5 proficiency in at least one of Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. CPAWSB uses "Management Accounting" for the Competency Map's management decision-making and information systems and technology area. W11W9
WestUnder CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026), Foundational Experience may be entry-level but must require decision-making and judgment and cannot be clerical. It must show at least Level 2 proficiency in the Decision Process and may be drawn entirely from experience gained before the Foundational Development module. W11
WestCPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026) list three Foundational Task Statements: FTS1, prepare or explain information for input into internal or external reporting; FTS2, identify the users' needs and prepare practical alternatives or variance analysis; FTS3, explain analysis and findings in a transparent, understandable and professional manner. All three must be completed. W11
WestUnder CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026), prior experience is Foundational Experience, to a maximum of eight months net of leaves. It is recognized only if it falls within the five years immediately before the Foundational Development module, equals three or more full-time months and meets the minimum foundational competency requirements. W11
WestUnder CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026), a learner may accumulate Professional Experience once enrolled in the Foundational Development module, with a mentor in place and a qualifying Experience Plan submitted and approved by the provincial body. Professional Experience starts no earlier than the date the Experience Plan is submitted. W11
WestUnder CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026), the learner must gain experience in any two of the four Financial Reporting Task Statements or any two of the four Management Accounting Task Statements. The learner must also gain experience in all of the Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication statements. W11
WestThe Western draft policies define experience as relevant, paid, full- or part-time employment overseen by a mentor. Experience in academia and self-employment are excluded. W11
WestFor public accounting licensure in the West, the draft policies require at least 24 months of qualifying experience in Assurance and Trust within a registered or licensed CPA firm. The learner must also meet the task-based requirements in both Financial Reporting and Assurance and Trust and the chargeable hour requirements. W11
WestThe chargeable-hour requirements in CPAWSB's draft policies (May 2026) are: for Audit, at least 1,250 chargeable hours in assurance with a minimum of 625 in the audit of historical financial statements; for Review (where applicable), at least 1,250 in assurance with a minimum of 625 in audit or review of historical financial statements; for Compilation (where applicable), at least 625 chargeable hours in compilation. The hours can be met only in firms registered with a provincial or territorial body and licensed to provide public accounting. W11
WestIn the West, all experience requirements must be met before a learner is eligible for the CPA Professional Readiness module. W11W16
Atl.CPA Atlantic requires a minimum of 24 months of qualifying experience, excluding time away from work. It consists of up to 8 months of Foundational Experience and at least 16 months of Professional Experience. A7A1
Atl.In Atlantic Canada, time off such as vacation or holidays, and leaves of absence, do not count toward the 24 months. A1
Atl.Atlantic Foundational Work Experience can be completed before the Foundational Development module. It must fall within 5 years before starting that module, last at least 3 months and be completed before the experience plan is submitted. A7
Atl.Atlantic Foundational Work Experience requires three Foundational Task Statements in a CPA Training Area, each at level 2 proficiency. Learners are expected to reach Level 2 by the end of the Foundational stage. A7A17
Atl.Atlantic Professional Work Experience can be gained while completing the Foundational Development module and must be completed before the Professional Readiness module. Learners are expected to reach Level 4 or Level 5 proficiency by the end of the Professional stage. A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic lists eight CPA Training Areas: Financial Reporting, Management Accounting, Assurance & Trust, Taxation, Finance, Strategy & Governance, Non-Financial Reporting and Big Data. Learners must work in roles that let them show the highest proficiency levels in Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. A7
Atl.For Professional Work Experience in Atlantic Canada, the learner chooses Financial Reporting or Management Accounting and must master any two of its four Professional Task Statements. The page says all decision competencies are mandatory, with Professional Skepticism and Ethical Decision Making required at level 5 and Communication at level 4. The Communication (DC3) task statement on the same page is labelled Level 5. A17
Atl.For the Atlantic licensure pathway, the CPA Training Areas must be Financial Reporting and Assurance & Trust, and the learner must also master the Assurance and Trust task statement. The supervisor or manager for foundational experience and the CPA Mentor for professional experience must be a registered Licensed Public Accountant, and the organization must be registered for public accounting with the provincial body. A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic says all 24 months and the required chargeable hours for licensure must be obtained within a firm registered to train students in external audit and/or review, where applicable. Its experience page says applicable chargeable hours are required. As of Nov 18, 2026 it gave no number of hours. A17A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic's transition policy defines new-program experience as relevant, paid full-time or part-time employment within a CPA training area, supervised by a CPA mentor. Experience in academia and self-employment are excluded. A5
New program: review process
ONIn Ontario all work experience is reported in CPA Ontario's Work Experience Management System (WEMS). Students submit their reports there and Foundational Work Experience Signatories and CPA Mentors submit their verification there. ON12
ONStep one in Ontario, if the student claims Foundational Work Experience: submit a Foundational Work Experience Report with the declaration of the FWE Signatory or CPA Mentor. It must be submitted before the Professional Work Experience (PWE) Work Plan. ON13
ONCPA Ontario's policies say a Foundational report for experience gained before registration should be submitted immediately on registration. For experience gained after registration it should be submitted within 30 days of the role ending or of reaching the eight-month maximum, whichever is earlier. ON12
ONAn Ontario FWE Signatory is a CPA Ontario member in good standing, or an equivalent member of a PTB or an IFAC member body. The Signatory must have worked for the same organization during the same period and hold a position senior to the student. ON13ON12
ONStep two in Ontario: while enrolled in or after the Foundational Development module, the student prepares a PWE Work Plan and submits it to the CPA Mentor for verification. The student then submits the plan with the mentor's declaration to CPA Ontario's Director of Employer Relations, who decides whether the experience is eligible. ON13
ONIn Ontario, Professional Work Experience completed up to 90 days before the PWE Work Plan is approved may be recognized only if it is otherwise eligible and is identified in the plan. ON13
ONAn Ontario CPA Mentor must be approved by CPA Ontario. Requirements include at least three years of post-qualification experience, CPA Mentor training, a signed CPA Mentor Contract, working for the same organization as the student and holding a position senior to the student. ON12
ONIt is the Ontario student's responsibility to find employment with an organization that employs at least one CPA and to find a CPA Mentor there. The student names the mentor in the PWE Work Plan, and the mentor's eligibility is assessed together with the plan. ON12
ONCPA Ontario's policies require the CPA Mentor to meet regularly with the student after the PWE Work Plan is approved and to give informal periodic evaluations. As of Nov 18, 2026 the policies stated no number of meetings. Mentors may not accept remuneration for the role. ON12
ONAn Ontario student is expected to keep the same CPA Mentor for the whole of their work experience. A change is approved only in extenuating circumstances. ON12
ONIf an Ontario student's employment changes during Professional Work Experience, the student submits an interim PWE report within 30 days of the change. The student reports the changes to the PWE Work Plan for approval within 90 days of starting any new employment. ON13
ONA change in employment in Ontario includes a different position, a change in work hours such as full time to part time, a change in CPA Training Area, a change in the Financial Reporting or Management Accounting learning outcomes, and a change in CPA Mentor. ON12
ONFinal step in Ontario: the student submits a Professional Work Experience Report with the CPA Mentor's declaration for approval by the Director of Employer Relations. The report must be consistent with the approved PWE Work Plan and should be submitted within 30 days of completing the requirements. ON13ON12
ONIn the Ontario report the CPA Mentor declares that the student's experience meets the required Task Statements in either Financial Reporting or Management Accounting, and in Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication. ON12
ONIn Ontario the Work Experience Component is completed when the student's final PWE Report is approved. Students cannot enrol in the Professional Readiness module and examination until then. ON13
ONAn Ontario student who disagrees with the Director of Employer Relations' assessment of a PWE Work Plan or of the final review may appeal to the Admission and Registration Committee. The committee's decision is final. ON13
ONOntario CPA Mentors and FWE Signatories must keep all records related to the work experience for at least seven years from the date of their declaration. ON12
QCThe Order monitors the new program's practical experience only at the beginning and at the end, using two tools: the work plan and the practical experience report. QC6QC14
QCStep one in Quebec: the candidate submits a work plan in their online file with the Order within 90 days of starting the practical experience. Experience declared after that deadline might not be recognized and may be subject to administrative fees. QC14
QCThe Quebec work plan must be approved by the CPA mentor and by the Order. If the candidate did practical experience before registering, the plan must also be approved by a CPA member in good standing at the organization where that experience took place. QC14
QCFrom the work plan, the Order decides whether the experience is foundational or professional, based on when it was acquired, the responsibilities of the role, the complexity of the situations and the competencies to be developed. QC29QC14
QCIf the Order assesses post-registration experience as foundational, it sets a time limit, because at most 8 months of foundational experience is accepted. At the end of that period the candidate must request a re-evaluation in the online file so that the rest can be recognized as professional. QC14
QCIf the Order recognizes 8 months of experience from before registration, the remaining 16 months must be recognized as professional work experience. QC14
QCFinal step in Quebec: the candidate submits a practical experience report in the online file within 30 days of the end of the 24 months, the end of a job, or a change of job. The report must be approved by the CPA mentor and by the Order. QC14
QCThe Order says the type of experience finally recognized is determined by its analysis of the practical experience report at the end. Under the regulation, the Order decides within 90 days of receiving the end-of-stage report, and the candidate may request a review within 30 days of receiving a decision that they do not meet the stage requirements. QC6QC12
QCFor Quebec experience completed after registration, a CPA mentor must accompany the candidate throughout, whether the experience is foundational or professional. The mentor must be a member in good standing of the Order, work in the same organization, approve the work plan and approve the experience reports. QC6
QCIf no CPA works in the Quebec organization, the candidate may ask a CPA from their network to act as mentor. This applies only to experience that does not lead to the public accountancy permit. QC6
QCThe Order's page for mentors asks the mentor to approve the work plan within 90 days of the start and to attest to the experience within 30 days of the end. It describes the commitment as about fifteen hours a year per trainee, and the mentor may not charge fees. QC31
QCThe Order's mentor page says the program monitors the experience at two points, and that organizations are free to add periodic follow-up meetings or informal evaluations. As of Nov 18, 2026 it stated no required number of mentor meetings. QC31
QCIf a Quebec candidate's tasks, responsibilities or role change significantly, the candidate must notify the Order promptly, and the Order may ask for a new work plan or a report. A change of mentor is recorded in the online file. QC14
QCThe Order may apply closer monitoring than the standard process in certain situations, and says it will contact the candidate if so. QC6
QCQuebec's regulation, in force January 1, 2027, requires the candidate to apply for authorization of the stage project before starting a stage or any new period with a new employer. The project must be validated and signed by the stage supervisor, and the Order may recognize up to 8 months of relevant experience from the 5 years before registration. QC12
WestThe Western draft policies (May 2026) say learners must, at a minimum, submit three pieces of reporting: a Foundational Experience report, either with the Experience Plan or on its own in advance; an Experience Plan at the beginning of Professional Experience; and an Experience Completion Report at the end of Professional Experience. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), the Experience Plan must show how the learner will reach the highest proficiency in Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. The CPA Mentor must approve it and the provincial body also reviews and approves it. Any Foundational Experience must be submitted before or with the plan. W11W9
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), Foundational Experience must be attested to by a CPA or IFAC designate who is senior to the learner and worked at the organization during the experience. A learner starting Foundational Experience can send a job description to the provincial body, which will advise whether it qualifies. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), every learner needs a CPA Mentor at all times during Professional Experience, and experience cannot be recognized while the learner has none. The mentor must be a CPA in good standing, work for the same entity, hold a position senior to the learner, charge no fees and complete the provincial body's initial and ongoing mentor training. W11
WestThe Western mentor's listed duties are to approve the Experience Plan, monitor progress toward it, attest to the Professional Experience at completion, and keep supporting documentation until the learner is accepted into membership. As of Nov 18, 2026 the draft policies stated no meeting frequency. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), learners should report material changes to the provincial body within 30 days. These include a change in job, work hours or work arrangement, CPA Training Area, planned competencies or mentor, and a leave from employment. A job change before the learner has worked three months (net of leaves) in the role earns no duration or competencies. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), at the end the learner submits an experience completion report showing where the highest proficiency was reached in Financial Reporting or Management Accounting and in Professional Skepticism, Ethical Decision Making and Communication. The mentor attests, the provincial body assesses the report, and on approval the learner must proceed to register in Professional Readiness. W11
WestCPAWSB's key dates say learners can begin submitting work experience plans in early 2027. BC learners without a CPA mentor at their workplace are told to contact CPABC. W13BC3
WestCPABC says learners must follow an approved experience plan and be supported by a CPA mentor employed within their organization. It refers learners to the Western Region Education and Experience Policies for the requirements. W41
WestCPA Alberta describes the new model as including a work plan submitted before practical experience starts, a CPA mentor who validates the competencies gained, and reporting through a reporting system. As of Nov 18, 2026 the page did not name the system. W42
Atl.In Atlantic Canada a professional work plan must be created and approved by the learner's CPA Mentor and CPA Atlantic School of Business before Professional Work Experience can be gained. Learners may begin reporting experience when they start the Foundational Development module. A7A2
Atl.Atlantic Foundational Work Experience does not require a CPA Mentor, but it must be signed off by a CPA who works at the same organization. Professional Work Experience requires a CPA Mentor who works within the same organization. A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic says the CPA mentor supports and assesses the learner's progress against the approved work plan. Mentors are accountable for confirming that the learner completed the approved work plan and gained the proficiency needed. A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic says a CPA mentor in the new program is different from a mentor under the current requirements in PERT. It said more information on mentor requirements would be shared later in 2026. A7
New program: employer programs and pre approved positions
ONCPA Ontario keeps pre-populated PWE Work Plans, approved for specified roles in specific organizations, in the WEMS library. A student may use one if it exists for their role. Otherwise the student prepares a new plan with the CPA Mentor and submits it for approval. ON12ON5
ONFor licensure, Ontario's policies provide for External Audit Training Offices. These are firms approved by CPA Ontario to deliver external audit training to students who want to be eligible for a Public Accounting Licence on admission to membership. ON12
ONStudents employed in an Ontario External Audit Training Office have a CPA Mentor assigned to them. Pre-populated PWE Work Plans approved for external audit roles in approved Training Offices are in the WEMS library. ON12
ONTo be approved as an Ontario Training Office, a firm must be in good standing and, for new applications, have completed a practice inspection that did not result in a reinspection or a referral to the Professional Conduct Committee. CPA Ontario sets a limit on the number of students a Training Office may employ, based on the assurance hours available. ON12
ONCPA Ontario stopped accepting Pre-Approved Program applications and program modifications after January 31, 2026, except for External Audit. Its employer page says students can submit their experience through the Experience Verification Route instead. ON32
QCFor public accountancy, the Order accredits firms as public accountancy training environments under the new program. The stated purpose is to let trainees meet the practical experience requirements for a public accountancy permit. QC31
QCTo be accredited in Quebec, a firm must offer audit and review services on general-purpose financial statements and have had a professional inspection in audit and review without a reservation about hiring. A firm seeking accreditation only for the permit limited to review engagements does not have to offer audit services. QC31
QCEach accredited Quebec firm must designate a person responsible for its training environment, who must hold the CPA auditor title. That person does not approve work plans or reports, which is the mentors' responsibility. QC31
QCThe Order may limit the number of public accountancy trainees in an accredited firm. It said a new accreditation form would be available in fall 2026 and that, until then, firms should complete the current questionnaire for pre-approved public accountancy programs. QC31
QCThe Order calls 24 months in an accredited public accountancy training environment an accelerated path to the permit. It says other relevant firm experience that meets the public accountancy regulation can also lead to the permit, through a request for evaluation once the person is a CPA member. QC30
QCThe Order's new-program employer page says trainees are responsible for finding a mentor among the CPAs in the organization, and asks organizations to structure positions that allow the required competencies to develop. As of Nov 18, 2026 it described no pre-approved program outside public accountancy. QC31
WestThe Western draft policies provide for "pre-reviewed positions". An organization may ask the provincial body to pre-review one or more specific Experience Plans, and a plan and its position may be recognized as pre-reviewed at the provincial body's discretion. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), for each pre-reviewed Experience Plan the organization must designate a senior leader who is a CPA in good standing, provide structured training positions that develop the required competencies within 16 months of Professional Experience, and assign the learner a mentor. It must also permit reasonable time away from work to write program examinations. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), a provincial body may limit the number of learners under a pre-reviewed Experience Plan, and each plan is monitored on a risk-adjusted basis. Where a plan no longer complies with requirements, the provincial body may withdraw its pre-reviewed status. Experience obtained after the withdrawal date may not be recognized and affected learners must develop a new Experience Plan with the provincial body. W11
WestUnder the Western draft policies (May 2026), for a pre-reviewed Experience Plan in a public accounting stream the senior leader must be a CPA authorized to practise public accounting in that stream. The senior leader gives formal signoff to the provincial body when a learner completes or leaves the plan. W11
WestCPAWSB's comparison says the current program offers a pre-approved program or experience verification route, while in the new program all learners complete an experience plan submitted in advance. CPA Alberta says all learners will follow the same program and meet the same requirements. W16W42
Atl.As of Nov 18, 2026, CPA Atlantic's new-program experience page did not describe a pre-approved route for the new program. It named the Pre-Approved Program Route only in menu links, in the transition guidance for current candidates and in its contact form. For transitioning candidates it requires a CPA approved mentor within the organization, and says an external mentor may be considered case by case in extenuating circumstances, subject to approval. A7
Atl.CPA Atlantic's list of Pre-Approved Program Route offices describes these programs as designed for candidates in the current CPA PEP, to provide all required practical experience within 30 months. A18
Current program: requirements and the two routes
ONIn Ontario's current program, students need a minimum of 30 months of qualifying practical experience. They must meet requirements of core, depth, breadth and progression over six technical competency areas and five enabling competency areas. ON31
ONOntario's current core requirement is any three sub-competencies in Financial Reporting and/or Management Accounting at Level 1 or higher. Depth is all sub-competencies in one of the six areas, with at least two at Level 2. ON31
ONOntario's current breadth requirement is at least eight sub-competencies, with at least four at Level 2 and the rest at Level 1 or higher. All five enabling competencies must reach Level 2 by the end. ON31
ONOntario's current program has two routes. In the Pre-Approved Program Route (PPR) the student is in a formal training program approved by CPA Ontario to meet all requirements within 30 months. In the Experience Verification Route (EVR) the student's job position is pre-assessed by CPA Ontario before reporting can begin. ON25
ONIn Ontario's current program, PPR students report to CPA Ontario only at the end of the training program or when they change employers or leave the program. EVR students report at specific times and when they change employers or roles. All students meet their mentor at least twice a year and report in PERT. ON25
ONUnder Ontario's current program, Regulation 17-1 sets licensure experience at 30 months in an Approved Training Office in an External Audit Pre-Approved Program, with a minimum of 2,500 chargeable hours. These include 1,250 chargeable hours in assurance services, of which at least 625 are in the audit of historical financial information and 100 are review procedures, plus 1,250 eligible hours in public accounting or designated services. ON15
QCQuebec's current program sets the practical experience at a minimum of 24 months in total, full time at a minimum of 32 hours per week or part time at a minimum of 17.5 hours. Up to 8 months from the 5 years before registration can be recognized, and at least 16 months must follow the start of the Professional Education Program. QC32
QCQuebec's current core requirement is at least Level 1 in three Financial reporting and/or Management accounting sub-areas. Depth is Level 2 in at least two sub-areas of the chosen competency and at least Level 1 in its others. Breadth is Level 2 in at least four sub-areas and at least Level 1 in four others. QC33
QCQuebec's current program offers a pre-approved program, the experience verification route, or a combination. In a pre-approved program the duties are analyzed before the candidate starts and a CPA program leader assigns them. On the experience verification route any employer can hire a trainee, but that path does not qualify for a public accountancy permit. QC32
QCIn Quebec's current program the candidate declares the start of the practical experience in the online file within 60 days of the first day of work. The candidate writes two reports for each 12 months worked and has two meetings a year with the CPA mentor. QC32
QCUnder Quebec's current program, the CPA auditor path requires the entire 24 months in a pre-approved program in audit at a firm recognized by the Order. It carries the same 1,250 assurance hours, including 625 hours in audit of general-purpose financial statements. QC30
WestThe West's current program requires a minimum of 30 months of qualifying practical experience, inclusive of up to 5 months away from work. CPA Alberta describes the allowance as up to 20 weeks of time away. W16W43
WestIn the West's current program, candidates must develop breadth and depth of technical competencies and develop the enabling competencies. CPABC lists the requirement as demonstration of core, depth and breadth technical competencies. W24W44
WestThe West's Experience Verification Route lets the candidate choose the employer but requires more reporting: detailed experience reports in PERT, reviewed by the profession at key milestones and verified by supervisors. Pre-approved programs are training positions approved in advance and designed to meet the requirements within 30 months, with review when the candidate completes the program. W24
WestIn the West's current program, qualifying experience for the audit and review streams of public accounting can be gained only through pre-approved programs. Candidates must meet their CPA mentor at least semi-annually. W24
Atl.Atlantic Canada's current program requires a minimum of 30 months of relevant experience, gained within a seven-year rolling window. Candidates must show competency in technical competencies through core, depth and breadth, show competency in enabling competencies and maintain mentorship. A13
Atl.In the Atlantic Pre-Approved Program Route, the candidate is assigned a mentor through the employer and completes specific competencies approved by the profession and the employer. In the Experience Verification Route, CPA Atlantic assesses and approves the position, and the candidate finds their own mentor. A13
Atl.A relevant Atlantic EVR position must allow experience in at least two technical sub-competency areas at Level 1 or higher. Current candidates must meet their mentor semi-annually. A13

blocks.sx-attempts:
Every body allows three attempts at a module examination ON20QC17W48A12. Ontario deregisters a student 45 days after the result of a third unsuccessful attempt and reregisters only in extraordinary circumstances ON33ON33. In the West and Atlantic a candidate who transitions has up to three attempts per module and exam regardless of prior attempts, and in Quebec a candidate who fails the last CFE can transition provided it was not the third and final attempt W12A5QC1.

Show
TopicOntarioCPA OntarioQuebecOrdre des CPA du QuébecWestCPA Western School of BusinessAtlanticCPA Atlantic School of Business
Attempt limits and what follows the last failed attempt
Attempts at module examsA student is deregistered after a third unsuccessful attempt at Core 1, Core 2, Capstone 1 or Capstone 2. After an unsuccessful module examination the student may write a challenge examination or repeat the module and examination, and may request a re-mark. ON20ON20Three attempts to pass each examination. After a first failed attempt at a core or elective module the module need not be retaken; after a second, it must be retaken. QC17CPAWSB: three attempts in total at a module examination, whether the later attempts are exam rewrites or full module retakes. W48CPA Atlantic: three attempts in total at a module examination, whether the later attempts are exam rewrites or full module retakes. A12
After a third failed module attemptThe Registrar deregisters the student 45 days after the release of the result of the third unsuccessful attempt. A deregistration under section 47.5 is excluded from the decisions a student may appeal to the Admission and Registration Committee. ON33ON20ON33After a third failed attempt at a core module, an elective module or Capstone 1 the candidate is expelled from the CPA program and may not re-enrol in any module unless the file is submitted for review and re-entry is granted. QC17CPAWSB: after three unsuccessful attempts at a core module exam the candidate is removed from CPA PEP and may apply for re-admission. CPABC Bylaw 405.1: enrollment is cancelled once all permitted opportunities are exhausted; the Registrar or the educational body may grant an additional opportunity. W48W49[OPEN – the CPA Atlantic pages checked did not state what happens after a third failed attempt at a module…]
After a third failed CFEDeregistered 45 days after the result of a third unsuccessful CFE attempt; if an appeal of the CFE result was filed, immediately when the appeal is denied. This deregistration cannot be appealed to the Admission and Registration Committee (only exception named: the September 2024 writing). ON33ON33The Order sends an exclusion notice. If no re-mark is requested it arrives 10 business days after the re-mark request deadline; the notice gives a date by which a letter of justification may be emailed. QC34CPA Alberta's Directives (effective February 27, 2025) state that only CPAWSB may grant special permission for a fourth attempt at the CFE. CPABC Bylaw 405.1 cancels enrollment once all permitted opportunities are exhausted, unless an additional opportunity is granted. W50W49[OPEN – the CPA Atlantic pages checked did not state the number of CFE attempts allowed or what happens after a…]
Three failures at an electiveAfter three unsuccessful attempts no further attempts at that module or examination can be made. Students who cannot successfully complete two electives are deregistered. ON20A third failed attempt at an elective module leads to expulsion from the CPA program, with no re-enrolment in any module unless the file is submitted for review and re-entry is granted. QC17CPAWSB: a candidate unsuccessful after three attempts at one elective exam can still attempt another elective in which three attempts have not been used. Two of the four electives must be passed to reach Capstone 1. W48[OPEN – not stated by this body]
What counts as an attemptAn unsuccessful attempt includes a failure as determined by the Board of Examiners and a failure to attend a scheduled examination, module or mandatory workshop on time or at all. For the CFE, withdrawing before the scheduled start of the first writing day and not attending is not counted. ON33ON36[OPEN – not stated by this body]CPAWSB's transition page warns that a withdrawal may count as an unsuccessful attempt depending on timing. W15[OPEN – not stated by this body]
What is lost on removalA deregistered student loses student rights and privileges, any transitional or special considerations awarded, credits, courses and any reported practical experience. ON34[OPEN – not stated by this body]CPAWSB lists exhausting module or examination attempts among the grounds on which a candidate may be suspended or withdrawn. In its section on candidates who ask to withdraw permanently, it says permanent withdrawal results in loss of credit for all completed modules and of recognized practical experience. W45[OPEN – not stated by this body]
If the candidate transitions before the next attempt
Do used attempts carry over[OPEN – the regulations, policies and transition pages checked did not state whether attempts used under…]A candidate who fails the last CFE (September 2028) can transition, provided it was not the third and final attempt, and then has a maximum of three attempts at each exam in the new program. QC1At the point of entry to the new program a candidate has up to three attempts per module and per exam, regardless of any prior exam attempts in the current program. The CPAWSB FAQ adds "if their time limit allows". W12W17W15Candidates have three attempts per module and per exam in the new program, regardless of any prior attempts in the current program. The CPA Atlantic FAQ adds "if their time limit allows". A5A1A3
Entry point with CFE partly passedA student who transitions before passing the CFE must, at a minimum, complete the Professional Readiness module and Professional Final Exam III. Exemptions depend on the current-program components already passed (Regulation 9-4, section 12). ON6ON14Day 1 passed only: skips the first module and its exam and the two professional modules, but must pass those two modules' exams, then take Préparation à la pratique CPA and pass its exam. Days 2 and 3 passed only: also skips those two exams. QC7QC7A candidate who has passed CFE Day 1 only enters at Professional Final Exam I. A candidate who has passed Days 2 and 3 only enters at the CPA Professional Readiness module, exempt from Professional Final Exams I and II. W12A candidate who has passed CFE Day 1 only enters at Professional Final Exam I. A candidate who has passed Days 2 and 3 only enters at the CPA Professional Readiness module, exempt from Professional Final Exams I and II. A5
Transition is finalOnce a student has transitioned, Regulation 9-3 governs and the student cannot transition back to the current program. ON14[OPEN – not stated by this body]Once a transition application is processed the move is final and the candidate cannot return to the current program. A candidate approved to transition during the transition period does not have to reapply or meet the new program's entrance requirements. W12W17An eligible candidate can choose to transition before the final offering of the next CPA PEP module or exam. Once the application is approved and confirmed the candidate cannot return to the current program. A4
If the candidate stays in the current program
Rewriting a failed CFEA student who fails only part of the CFE may rewrite only that part at a future CFE (Day 1 alone, or Days 2 and 3 together). Retaking Capstone 2 is not required. ON35After a first or second failed result the candidate may write again at a later CFE. All three days are rewritten together if all were failed; otherwise only Day 1, or only Days 2 and 3 together. QC35CPAWSB: an unsuccessful candidate retakes only the failed part: Day 1 alone if only Day 1 was failed, both Day 2 and Day 3 if either was failed, and all three days in the same offering if all were failed. W47[OPEN – not stated by this body]
How long they can stayUnless otherwise provided in Regulation 9-4 or 9-1, students registered before January 1, 2027 have until December 31, 2028 to complete the current program or transition. To remain eligible to write the CFE or to transition, a person must be registered by December 31, 2026. ON14ON6A candidate already in the current program in 2027 must continue in it until December 2028, unless the university no longer offers it or the remaining National Program modules are no longer offered. QC7An eligible candidate who cannot finish because a required module or examination is no longer available must apply to transition. A candidate who chooses not to transition may remain only while a viable path to finish exists. W12W17A candidate can continue until the needed module or exam is no longer offered and must then transition; everyone must transition by December 2028. Candidates not eligible to transition must finish within the original time limit, subject to remaining offerings and attempts. A3A4A3
After a third failure: transition and readmission
Can they still transitionA student with two unsuccessful attempts who is awaiting the result of a third CFE attempt is not eligible to transition. No student may transition between an examination date and the release of its results. Section 11's list of ineligible students does not name section 47.5. ON14ON14ON14A candidate who fails the last CFE can transition provided it was not the third and final attempt. If it was the third attempt, the candidate is expelled from the program under the Order's current policy. QC1QC1Candidates who have reached the maximum number of CFE attempts are not eligible to transition. Eligibility also requires a time limit ending after December 31, 2028 and active status in good standing; exhausting exam attempts may affect standing and eligibility. W47W12W15To be eligible to transition a candidate must, among other conditions, have a current-program time limit ending after December 31, 2028 and hold active candidate status in good standing with their provincial body at the time of transition. A5
Getting back inReregistration only in extraordinary circumstances, at the discretion of the Registrar, the Admission and Registration Committee or the Appeal Committee, on conditions they set. The request needs a written explanation with documents; circumstances must be external, unanticipated and beyond the individual's control. ON33ON34ON34Once the file is closed, the candidate must apply for re-enrolment and pay the fees. The comité d'accès à la profession sets the steps, which could include redoing the whole professional education program; conditions are given if the application is accepted. QC34QC1A person who has exhausted all attempts at modules or module examinations can apply for re-admission to CPA PEP to restart the program, with a new valid transcript assessment. No more than 12 months of prior experience is recognized; the six-year education and seven-year experience limits reset. How each body names its categories

OntarioCategories used by CPA Ontario
CPA Ontario sorts foreign accounting bodies into five groups: Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs), reciprocal membership bodies, recognized accounting bodies, Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), and all other professional accounting bodies. ON37

CPAWSB names three groups of foreign accounting bodies:
  • bodies with a Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) or Reciprocal Membership Agreement (RMA) with Canada's CPA provincial bodies
  • organizations with a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
  • and member organizations of the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC). CPAWSB does not list the MRA and RMA bodies itself. It tells those applicants to apply through their provincial CPA body, not CPAWSB.
W36W56

The Ordre des CPA du Québec has three profiles for members of foreign bodies with an agreement:
  • the reciprocity agreement profile
  • the Quebec-France mutual recognition agreement (MRA), for members of the Ordre des experts-comptables de France
  • and the Quebec-Tunisia professional qualifications recognition agreement (PQRA), for members of the Ordre des Experts Comptables de Tunisie.
QC24

CPA Atlantic School of Business names three groups:

  • and IFAC member bodies with no MRA, RMA or MOU. It does not list the MRA and RMA bodies itself.
A15

CPA Nova Scotia defines three agreement types. An MRA specifies the right to membership between the two bodies and the process to obtain the right to practise public accounting. An RMA provides the right to membership between the two bodies. An MOU specifies the criteria by which members of one body are eligible for membership in the other. A19

  • CPA Canada defines an MRA as an agreement that specifies the right to membership between two bodies and the process to obtain the right to practise public accounting

blocks.gloss:
Board of Examiners
In Ontario's Regulation 9-3, the committee whose specific purpose is to oversee all examinations delivered in order to meet requirements toward membership and licensure. The national Exam Guide says the Board of Examiners sets the passing standard for candidates' performance on each exam. ON13N1
Capstone 1
In CPA PEP, the integrative module in which candidates use the knowledge from prerequisite and earlier modules in a professional, team setting to deepen strategic leadership competencies. Candidates complete a large business case, which relates to Day 1 of the CFE. W22
Capstone 2
In CPA PEP, the examination preparation module, which focuses on preparing for the Common Final Examination (CFE). Candidates apply the competencies acquired throughout the program in complex and highly integrative cases. W22
Common Final Examination (CFE)
The three-day examination that is the culmination of the CPA Professional Education Program (CPA PEP). It evaluates students on the competencies defined by the Competency Map. ON22
Core 1 and Core 2
The two core modules of CPA PEP, whose focus is breadth. Core 1 focuses on financial reporting, audit and assurance, finance, and taxation; Core 2 focuses on management accounting, finance, strategy and governance, and financial reporting. W22
CPA Atlantic School of Business
The body, abbreviated CPA ASB, that handles education delivery for CPA Nova Scotia, CPA New Brunswick, CPA Newfoundland and Labrador, . Its current-program page says CPA PEP is delivered locally by CPA Atlantic School of Business in Atlantic Canada. A2A10A5
CPA Core – Common
The version of the CPA Core module that develops the Advanced Professional Competencies and builds on learners' Specific Competencies in assurance and trust, big data and data analytics, and tax; its exam is two to three cases written in three hours. Ontario's Regulation 9-3 calls the exam Professional Final Examination 1A (common path), and Quebec describes the Common path as meant for those who want the CPA designation but do not want a public accountancy permit. N2N1ON13QC3
CPA Core – Licensure
The version of the CPA Core module for learners who are considering a public accounting licence; it includes the content of CPA Core – Common and develops certain Specific Competencies to a higher level of proficiency and complexity. Its exam has two parts, Part A (two to three cases, three hours) and Part B (one two-hour case). Quebec calls this module CPA Core – Common + Public accountancy, and Ontario's Regulation 9-3 calls the exam Professional Final Examination 1B (licensure). N2N1QC1ON13
CPA Leadership
The module that follows CPA Core, in which learners further develop their CPA Ethical Mindset and develop the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies to a higher proficiency level by applying the decision process to real-world challenges. Its exam (Professional Final Exam 2) is one five-hour comprehensive case. N2N1
CPA PEP
The CPA Professional Education Program: the graduate-level program that makes up the educational portion of the current CPA certification program, consisting of a series of modules culminating in the three-day Common Final Examination. It is composed of two core modules, two elective modules and two capstone modules. In Quebec, the PEP consists of modules (the National Program) or courses (the graduate program). ON17W22QC16
CPA Professional Readiness
The final module, in which learners hone their CPA Ethical Mindset and develop the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies to the highest level of proficiency; learners must meet all practical experience requirements before they take it. Its exam (Professional Final Exam 3) is one two-hour case focused on professional judgment and one one-hour case focused on ethical decision-making. N2N1
CPAWSB
The CPA Western School of Business. Western Canada's draft policies say it administers the CPA Professional Program for learners in the Western Region, and its current-program page says it delivers CPA PEP in Western Canada while the provincial bodies administer the experience requirements. W11W33
electives
The CPA PEP elective modules, which provide the opportunity to explore two fields of interest in greater depth; candidates must choose two. Candidates pursuing a career in public accounting must take Assurance and Tax. W22
experience plan / work plan
Western Canada's draft policies define the Experience Plan as a plan that learners develop, have signed off by the Mentor and submit to their PTB, outlining how they will achieve and demonstrate the highest level of proficiency in the Decision Process to satisfy the Professional Experience requirements. Ontario calls it the PWE Work Plan (the plan for Professional Work Experience), Atlantic calls it a professional work plan, and Quebec names the work plan as one of its two experience monitoring tools. W11ON13A7QC6
experience verification route
In the current program's practical experience, the route (EVR) in which students have their job position pre-assessed by CPA Ontario before they can begin reporting. Western Canada describes it as giving flexibility in the role but requiring more reporting: the candidate chooses the employer and completes detailed experience reports in PERT. ON25W24
Foundational Development (module)
The first module of the CPA Professional Program, in which learners develop Specific, Foundational, and Sub-Foundational Competencies and begin to develop the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies. Quebec describes it as the first module, which lays the foundations for the rest of the CPA path. N2QC3
Foundational Development Exam (module exam)
The exam for the Foundational Development module: 50 small objective-format questions (33% of the exam) and 4-8 testlets (67%), written in five hours. Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines the Foundational Development Examination as the CPA Ontario examination students must successfully complete on completion of the Foundational Development Module, or the equivalent evaluation offered by an Accredited Post-Secondary Institution. N1ON13
Foundational experience
Entry-level experience in the new program that requires decision-making and the application of judgment. Ontario calls it Foundational Work Experience (FWE): up to a maximum of 8 months of the required 24 months of Work Experience. W12ON13
Knowledge Assessment
A way for candidates who do not meet the necessary entrance requirements for the CPA Professional Program to demonstrate that they have the prerequisite knowledge and competencies; it consists of 150 objective-format questions written in five hours. Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines it as the examination used to assess a Student's expected entry level knowledge. N1ON13
mentor
Western Canada's draft policies define a Mentor as an experienced CPA who advises, counsels and guides learners. Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines a CPA Mentor as a Member in good standing of CPA Ontario (or an equivalent member of a PTB or of a listed member body) who meets the further requirements in the Work Experience policies, is approved, and oversees and attests to Work Experience; CPA Ontario notes that a CPA Mentor in the new program is different from a mentor in the current practical experience requirements. W11ON13ON5
MOU
Memorandum of Understanding. Western Canada's draft policies define it as a credential recognition agreement with an international accounting body that sets out the additional education, examination, or experience requirements under which members of one body may be eligible for membership in the other. W11
MRA / RMA
Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) and Reciprocal Membership Agreement (RMA). Western Canada's draft policies refer to them as agreements a PTB has with an international accounting body, a member of which may attest to experience a learner obtained outside Canada. W11
Ordre des CPA du Québec
The Ordre des comptables professionnels agréés du Québec, called "the Order" on its English pages. It delivers one of the two pathways for completing the CPA Professional Program in Quebec, accredits the universities that deliver the other pathway (the university graduate program), and recognizes candidates' practical experience. QC2QC5QC6
PERT
The Practical Experience Reporting Tool, in which current-program candidates report their practical experience. W12W24
post-secondary institution (PSI) / accredited program
Accredited programs are offered at select post-secondary institutions (PSIs) across Canada to deliver part of the CPA Professional Program; Western Canada's draft policies define a CPA Accredited Program as a program accredited to deliver all or part of the program, excluding the Professional Final Exams. Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines an Accredited Post-Secondary Institution as a Degree-Granting Institution that may be accredited to deliver Education Modules, the Foundational Development Examination, and/or the Programs set out in its Schedule A; in Quebec the equivalent pathway is the university graduate program, delivered by universities accredited by the Order. W20W11ON13QC5
pre-approved program route
In the current program's practical experience, the route (PPR) in which the student is part of a formal student training program that has been approved by CPA Ontario to meet all the requirements within 30 months. Western Canada describes pre-approved programs as training positions approved by the CPA profession in advance and designed to meet the practical experience requirements within 30 months. ON25W24
Professional experience
Experience in the new program which builds on Foundational Experience; it must be complex in nature, requiring the learner to apply Decision Competencies in more complex situations. Ontario calls it Professional Work Experience (PWE): a minimum of 16 months of the required 24 months of Work Experience. W12ON13
Professional Final Exam (Parts 1, 2, 3)
The national exams that test whether learners have achieved the required competencies for the CPA Professional Program, as defined in Western Canada's draft policies. The Exam Guide names CPA Core as Professional Final Exam 1, CPA Leadership as Professional Final Exam 2 and CPA Professional Readiness as Professional Final Exam 3; Ontario's Regulation 9-3 calls them the Part 1 (A or B), Part 2 and Part 3 Professional Final Examinations. W11N1ON13
proficiency level
Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines proficiency levels as the levels of proficiency at which Students are expected to demonstrate competence, as described in the CPA Competency Map. The Module Guide says the proficiency levels for the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies use verbs to identify the depth of competence on a scale of Level 1 to Level 5. ON13N2
PTB (provincial or territorial body)
Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines Provincial Territorial Bodies (PTBs) as the Chartered Professional Accountant bodies of all Canadian provinces, territories. Western Canada's draft policies define a PTB as a provincial or territorial or Bermudian CPA body. ON13W11
qualifying courses
In Ontario, the CPA Qualifying Courses are 15 courses (7 named courses and 8 additional business courses) that build the entry level knowledge required to enter the CPA Professional Program; a student who completes them through a listed post-secondary program is not required to take the Knowledge Assessment. Western Canada speaks of qualifying courses that may be used to meet the Knowledge Assessment exemption criteria, and its draft policies call the requirement Accounting and Business Knowledge, a minimum of 45 credit hours. ON13ON11BC4W11
task statements or training areas
Ontario's Regulation 9-3 defines a Task Statement as a description of prescribed activities in which a Student is required to have achieved the level of proficiency outlined in the Work Experience policies, and CPA Training Areas as relevant areas of work that provide the opportunity to gain necessary competencies. Western Canada's draft policies define Task Statements as statements that define the learning (educational and applied) outcomes by competency statement; Quebec says there are eight main training areas. ON13W11QC6
transition
The activity of a Candidate moving from the Current Program to the New Program. Western Canada's transition policies set the Transition Period as January 1, 2027, to December 31, 2028; in Ontario, students registered under Regulation 9-1 have until December 31, 2028 to complete the legacy program or transition to the CPA Professional Program. W12ON14
WEMS (Ontario's Work Experience Management System)
The CPA Ontario system in which all Work Experience is reported. Students are required to submit all Work Experience Reports in WEMS, and all employer verification (by FWE Signatories and CPA Mentors) is required to be submitted in WEMS. ON12

Quebec’s transition table is not charted here. The transition chart in this guide covers CPA Ontario, CPAWSB and CPA Atlantic. The Quebec Order publishes its own transition table, for guidance only; this guide reports its written scenarios but does not reproduce the table as a chart. QC7
Who approves a transition in Atlantic Canada. CPA Atlantic’s transition policy says a transition is not confirmed until approved by the Atlantic provincial body. Its transition FAQ says transition is confirmed only after the CPA Atlantic School of Business reviews and approves it. The two pages name different approvers. A4A3
“Launch” means different things. CPA Ontario says the program launches in January 2027; CPABC says May 2027. CPAWSB’s key dates put the start of the transition period at January 1, 2027, the first new-program modules in May 2027 and the first Professional Final Exams in September 2027. ON1BC1W1W13
Ontario prices and enrolment. As of Nov 18, 2026 CPA Ontario’s examination schedule page said enrolment details and fees for the examinations and modules “will be shared when available”. Its page on online and in-person study showed no tuition, said more details about enrolment “will be shared in late 2026”, and gave only “winter 2028” for the first Professional Readiness module. ON4ON2
Accreditation lists not final. Ontario’s university approval process was “anticipated to be completed in the fall”; Quebec’s lists were “subject to accreditation” in fall 2026, and for four Université du Québec campuses (our count) the page read “List will be available soon”. ON2QC5
Quebec fees, rules and the Knowledge Assessment. As of Nov 18, 2026 the Order’s “Costs, policies and rules” page read “Coming soon”; its page on the program it delivers gave module durations “for information purposes only”; and neither of those pages nor the new-program overview page mentioned a Knowledge Assessment. QC8QC2QC1
Western policies are a draft. The Education and Experience Policies are marked “Draft published May 2026”. The sections on regional transfers, advanced placement for accredited learners and international learners read “To come”, and the Learner Guide is due in early 2027. W11
Summary pages lag the schedules. CPAWSB’s key-date lists give months (“July 2028” for the last Capstone 2) while its schedule gives Aug 5, 2028; one page says final Core 1 registration closes in early November 2026 while the schedule shows Nov 23. CPA Atlantic’s overview mentions a Core 1 offering in May 2027 where the schedule shows an exam rewrite only. Use the dated schedules. W13W15W25A1
Atlantic details that differ between pages. The program description mentions a two-day in-person orientation, but the schedule lists the May 15–16, 2027 workshop as online. The new-program page names CPA Nova Scotia, CPA New Brunswick and CPA Newfoundland and Labrador among the bodies CPA ASB handles education delivery for, without naming Prince Edward Island; the Costs and Fees page names CPA Prince Edward Island as well, and the transition policy and the course lists also cover the province. A2A11A5A6
Sample exams may be revised. Sample cases “have not undergone the full range of processes and quality assurance checks”; corrected versions and full Knowledge Assessment and Foundational Development sample exams are due in early 2027. ON3W6
Western accredited master’s programs. CPAWSB says the University of Alberta MAcc and the University of Saskatchewan MPAcc will continue with advanced placement, but its policy section on accredited learners still reads “To come”. The University of Alberta says it “will not proceed with a new Master of Accounting intake in Spring 2027”. Saskatchewan’s brochure says students are exempt from the Foundational Development module and exam; no CPAWSB document confirms this or says which version of Exam 1 applies. W18W11X1U35 includes a non-CPA source
Who examines Ontario graduate-program students at the first stage. Regulation 9-3 exempts in-person graduates from the Foundational Development exam and lets an accredited university deliver an equivalent. University pages describe this differently: some say the exam is bypassed, Waterloo’s MAcc says students “write the Foundational Development examination”, and Queen’s says the assessment is administered by the school. Pages also differ on whether a program delivers CPA Core Common, Licensure or both. ON13U4U8U1U18 includes a non-CPA source
Ontario accreditation not confirmed school by school. CPA Ontario lists 17 institutions that applied for in-person accreditation but had not published approvals. University pages range from “under review” (Western DAN, York LA&PS) to “accredited” or “has received accreditation approval” (Ivey, Laurier, Guelph, Schulich). Toronto Metropolitan’s diploma takes its final intake in winter 2027 with no replacement page found; Ottawa and Lakehead show no redesigned program; Brock’s site could not be read; Toronto Mississauga’s MMPA is paused. ON2U6U15U13U25U12 includes a non-CPA source
Quebec and Atlantic university details. As of Nov 18, 2026 the Order’s page read “List will be available soon” for UQTR, UQAT, UQAC and UQAR, and all Quebec lists remain subject to accreditation. In Atlantic Canada, CPA Canada’s list (a 2023 Internet Archive copy) shows one accredited program, Saint Mary’s MBA-CPA Stream, which the university’s 2024–2025 calendar describes as accredited. On the same date CPA Atlantic’s new-program overview and program pages did not mention an accredited university program. QC5QC22N4U36A1A2 includes a non-CPA source
The national list of accredited programs is a 2023 snapshot. CPA Canada’s list of which CPA PEP modules each university program covers could only be read as a September 2023 copy from the Internet Archive. Programs have changed since (for example, Toronto Metropolitan was still listed as Ryerson). CPAWSB’s CFE page also lists Capstone 2 as a separate requirement, while the list shows the western master’s programs covering it. N4W21
